Mr. President, Ladies and Gentlemen, I rise to this
podium to honor the city of Caxias do Sul, which
celebrated its 121st anniversary yesterday, June 20. This
history began before Italian immigration, when drovers
passed through the area on their way between the southern
part of the state and the country's interior, and the
Caingangue Indians started to occupy the region, known
as Campo dos Bugres. During the second half of the 19th
century, economic hardships in Italy prompted immigration
to Brazil, starting in 1875.
The immigrants arrived in Campo dos Bugres
in 1876, and after two years, the area became known as
Colônia de Caxias. The Municipality of Caxias do Sul was
not founded until June 20, 1890.
From the beginning of its history to the present
day, the city has gone through various economic cycles,
which has allowed for the diversification of productive
activities. Among the first to gain prominence is the
cultivation of vines and wine production.
This grape and wine production continues to be
one of the city's main trademarks, also stimulating
tourism with the celebration of the largest festival in
the South, the Festival of the Grape.
These characteristics of Caxias do Sul are
determinant in boosting the other cities in the region
of Serra Gaúcha. We can say that Caxias do Sul has
developed and contributes to the development of the
cities surrounding it. And it is for this reason that its
prosperity is important for our Region, State, and Country.
I extend a special greeting to the citizens of
Caxias, who, with their dedication and commitment,
build prosperity in our region, which has high
development indices.
This development index can be seen in the
research conducted by the Brazilian Institute of
Geography and Statistics - IBGE, released last year,
on the economic performance of the 5,564 cities in
2008. The study positions Caxias do Sul as the 33rd
largest Gross Domestic Product in the country. This
result places the municipality ahead of seven capitals:
Florianópolis, Natal, Maceió, Cuiabá, Teresina,
Aracaju, and Campo Grande.
In the Southern Region, Caxias' performance
ranks 5th, behind only two capitals, Curitiba and Porto
Alegre, and the cities of Joinville and Canoas. This
picture demonstrates that the diversity of the city's
economic matrix drives positive results in the economy.

Randon, a company operating in the automotive

I have spoken about all this growth of our city to

Ladies and Gentlemen Deputies, the General Register of Employees and Unemployed - CAGED, disclosed yesterday that the country created 1 billion, 171,796 jobs from January to May of this year.

This number shows the wisdom of the Brazilian people, who voted for President Dilma to continue the economic policy being developed in Brazil. And this was not in vain. First, President Dilma continued, from an economic perspective; she even kept Finance Minister Guido Mantega; she politically articulated to ensure there would be no political jolt; and the government's continuity is working.

Therefore, this CAGED result shows the accuracy of the people's choice, as the hope that Brazil would continue to succeed is being confirmed. Only in the months of April and May, half a million new jobs were generated with signed contracts in Brazil. This is a demonstration that the country is heading in the right direction; it is the demonstration that Brazilian policy has command, has management. It was not in vain that President Dilma launched PAC 2.

What is PAC 2? It is an investment policy in infrastructure through which the government recognizes that Brazil, as it develops and grows, as various sectors of our economy suffer from a lack of infrastructure, needs works, investments in energy generation, roads, highways, ports, and airports.

For this reason, PAC 2 was launched, precisely to meet this logistics sector as quickly as possible.

But it doesn't stop there. There is a great concern from a social perspective. That's why President Dilma launched Minha Casa, Minha Vida, with the prediction of 2 billion new homes to meet an important portion of the population, mainly from classes C, D, and E, who do not have a home, do not have housing, but have the need to live in a dignified manner.

This is an ambitious program, an aggressive program of construction of popular homes, titled Minha Casa, Minha Vida, which also aims to stimulate the economy, because the construction materials sector has added value, and is the sector that generates the most jobs in Brazil.

And all this was conceived from the concern of there being qualification. It is necessary to qualify professionals. In Brazil, due to the long-standing economic stagnation, it is evident that we are starting to feel the lack of engineering professionals, technicians, doctors, in short, professionals from all areas.

And that's why it's important to accelerate the process of creating federal universities and technical institutes. Creating specific technical qualification programs must be an initiative of the Federal Government, together with State Governments, Municipalities, but also with the private sector.

So, it's a set of actions. And the winner is Brazil, the winner is the Brazilian people.

For all these reasons, there is Brazil's concern not only to control inflation, maintain economic and political stability, but also to improve the quality of life of the population. And we are referring to the population as a whole.

Also in this sense, there is the launch of programs with the objective of ending poverty in Brazil.
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES

Brazil, where there are still 16 million people without even the most basic resources for survival. This is also a strong, deep program that requires the participation of all citizens and citizens of this country, of civil society, of municipalities, and states.

In addition to this program, the Federal Government is also concerned with ensuring that all companies, all consortia, and indeed, all those who come to exploit the wealth of our country or who come to share in it, are welcome to bring their resources, but at the same time, that they generate jobs and bring technology.

We no longer want to be a country of cheap labor or a country of consumers; we no longer want to be just exporters of commodities and food; we want to be a country that produces science, technology, and art. We want to be a truly developed country in its fullness, where the quality of life of the people is in first place, where the people can be proud of their country. And that Brazil be, in the near future, the fifth largest economy in the world, increasingly respected abroad, as it is now.

Today, Brazil is heard on the major world issues, from the perspective of internal consumption as well as within the World Trade Organization; from the environmental perspective to the model of growth. That is why the G-8 no longer exists. The G-8 is over. Today there is the G-20. There has been an expansion of the countries that discuss the future of the planet, the future of humanity. And Brazil is part of this debate. Today, Brazil's opinion is not secondary, it is not the opinion of those who simply complain and who no one listens to. Today, Brazil is heard abroad thanks to an aggressive policy of income distribution, thanks to a behavior of dignity, maturity, that began with President Lula. And now President Dilma is continuing this Brazil that is the pride of all of us.

It is obvious, Mr. President - I return to what I said at the beginning - that this is due to the wisdom of the Brazilian people. The Brazilian people realize that they have a government that works with seriousness; they realize that they have a government that speaks firmly abroad; they realize that they have a government that is concerned with economic growth, but turned towards sustainable growth, towards environmental preservation; they realize that they have a government that is concerned with income distribution, primarily through the valorization of the minimum wage, which we voted on in this House and which has a very clear rule until 2014.

The recovery of the minimum wage takes place, first, by recompensing what inflation erodes and, second, taking into consideration the Gross Domestic Product. The recovery of the minimum wage is, therefore, a process that takes into account both the economic context and the social context.

So, this rule ensures that every year, the minimum wage
undergoes actual appreciation.
The Brazilian people perceive the concern for income distribution
through Bolsa Família and, now, through the poverty alleviation plan
recently launched;
the Brazilian people perceive the concern for ensuring adequate
pension, especially for those who retire, so they can live with dignity.
So, this is the model of country we are building. And this Parliament
cannot deny helping President Dilma. That is what we have to do.
There are several topics we need to deepen, debate, discuss in this House,
such as, for example, political reform, which is stalled. We hope that
soon the Special Commission will present its report, and we can discuss
in this plenary the appropriate political reform for this modern country.
We also need to carry out a tax reform that de-burdens the payroll
and, at the same time, generates jobs. We need to create more efficient
control mechanisms, so that public resources can really be applied
to what is most needed.
That is why President Dilma and all the workers who, through their
effort, competence, and dignity, achieved the jobs indicated by the
Labor Ministry, deserve congratulations. From January to May,
1,171,796 jobs is not a small thing for those who have needs and
need to support their families.
This is the government that is working. Let's continue it so that
this happens more and more.

Eternal penalty for the torture, the genocide they practiced, and the permanent disrespect and violations of human rights. Here, in Brazil, with the support of a complicit media, they are pushing things along slowly. We will not turn the page of history.

Our children and young people need to know the truth, to understand what happened in the dungeons of military dictatorship—the lack of freedom, censorship, assassinations, torture methods, and state terrorism that existed in our country.

That is why we do not want the Truth Commission to be conducted lightly here, but that it truly has a public clarification.

Mr. President, I also take this opportunity to say that finally the news has emerged about the control of land purchases in Brazil by foreigners. It is on the front page of today's Estado de S. Paulo: "Foreigners buying more than 5 hectares will need government approval."

Nowadays, thousands of hectares of land are being purchased by foreigners for soybean cultivation in the Amazon and Northeast. It is absolute chaos. An individual can buy up to 50 fiscal modules. According to the proposal, the limit would be reduced to 15 fiscal modules, between 75 and 1,500 hectares—that is for individuals. That is already a lot of land for a foreigner. And for companies as well.

The Presidency of the Republic does not need to apologize, saying that we are avoiding foreign investment. This is about the Brazilian land, the strategic planning of the use of Brazilian land, and we should indeed set limits.

I hope that this law comes to this House so that we can discuss with rigor the true foreign invasion in Brazil.

MR. MAURO MARIANI (PMDB-SC. Without revision by the speaker.)—Mr. President, ladies and gentlemen, in my statement, I highlight an action by the municipality of São Bento do Sul in the environmental area.

Since March of this year, the municipality of São Bento do Sul has been paying rural landowners who maintain Permanent Preservation Areas (APP). Through a decree of the mayor, the municipality begins to pay those rural producers who maintain Permanent Protection Areas and Legal Reserves in water sources through their water company.

This is the type of example that needs to be brought to this House, because it can be a good example for the country when the discourse and debate on the environment become heated. But few practices like that of São Bento do Sul are carried out.

So, I would like to congratulate the entire community of São Bento do Sul.

Mr. President, ladies and gentlemen deputies, good initiatives should be recognized and passed on, especially in today's days, when these practices aim to address and mitigate environmental problems caused by the human species in its quest for development, leaving natural resources threatened.

That is why I bring to this House the example of the city of São Bento do Sul, located in the northern plateau of Santa Catarina. There, the city hall will financially support landowners who maintain or recover their Legal Reserve areas in properties along the Red River.

The Environmental Services Payment Program - PSA, in São Bento do Sul, became a reality on March 22, 2011, when a decree was signed by Mayor Magno Bollmann, not coincidentally, on Water Day.

The PSA will correct the omission in the pricing of environmental services and make the conservation of forests an economic option. Basically, the idea is to remunerate those who preserve, directly or indirectly, the environment. Initially, 49 landowners who affect the water source that supplies the municipality may receive for their preservation. Each landowner must register, the property undergoes an inspection, and finally, they sign the contract. The plots are evaluated by a commission and 18 requirements are analyzed. The payment is made according to the score.

The creation of the PSA will bring socio-environmental gains, while ensuring the conservation of natural resources and improving the quality of life of people.

São Bento do Sul is the first municipality in Santa Catarina to implement the PSA. The measure will ensure water supply for over 75,000 inhabitants. The carbon credit market, implemented by the Kyoto Protocol, is the most widespread PSA project in the world. However, there are several other conservation projects and public policies, including in Brazil.

There are projects in the Chamber that deal with rewarding those who preserve the environment, such as Bills of Law Nos. 792, of 2007, 5,487, of 2009, and 1,274, of 2011.

The first initiatives in this regard emerged in the 1990s in Costa Rica, which created a system of taxing fuel and water to, with resources raised, remunerate landowners of preserved properties.

If development is inevitable and necessary, we should encourage actions that minimize the impacts and damages caused to the environment.

Thank you very much!
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES

Giving as read the statement regarding the political reform, the mother of all reforms, on which great expectations have been placed in this House. And Brazilian society as a whole also has this expectation. A commission has been established in this House and another in the Senate, and what we are seeing is that nothing will happen. By the looks of it, it will stay as it is. So, it is a great disappointment and concern.

My statement is in this regard: to appeal for it to actually happen, both here in the Chamber and in the Senate, so that Brazilian society has a political reform that truly meets its interests.

Thank you, Mr. President.

STATEMENT SUBMITTED BY THE SPEAKER

Mr. President, Ladies and Gentlemen Deputies, I come to this podium to speak about "the mother of all reforms," political reform. I say this because the improvement of our electoral and party system is a necessary requirement for the continuity and the good progress of transformations in other dimensions of our social life.

As everyone knows, this is not a new topic, as this House has been systematically and permanently examining our electoral and party legislation. Many advances have already been made, such as the Law of Political Parties and the Law of Elections, laws promulgated in the 1990s, as well as recent improvements to Complementary Law No. 64 of 1990, the result of a broad social pressure process for greater ethics and transparency in the selection process of candidates for elective offices, known as the Clean Slate Amendment.

But society expects this House to do even more to perfect our political institutions. In this regard, there is a body of knowledge and debates based on the results produced by the Special Commissions that recently analyzed various political reform proposals.

One of them seems more consistent to me: the one that establishes closed party lists in proportional elections, provides for exclusive public financing, and prohibits coalitions in proportional elections. I would also suggest, as a topic to be debated by the Commission, the end of re-election for executive office holders and the coincidence of terms for all elective offices, with an increase in the term to 5 years.

I therefore believe that efficiency and transparency in public administration depend on the actual commitment of representatives to the interests of society.

The aspirations of the entire Brazilian population, something that will hardly be achieved if we continue using the private financing system for election campaigns.

I believe that the link between the reform and the improvement of our representative democracy needs to be clearly emphasized. Anyone who follows attentively the growing increase in the costs of election campaign activities knows that private influence has significantly increased in our electoral process. Candidates who are entirely dependent on private resources will not be able to fulfill their commitments to the entire population. Sooner or later, they will have to "account" to those who contributed decisively to their electoral success, either through support for projects that serve the specific interests of certain groups or even by sponsoring questionable proposals to various federal public administration bodies, in order to favor these same sponsors.

At the same time, the establishment of exclusive public financing should be accompanied by a specific change in our proportional list representation system, which should transition from the current open list to a previously ordered list by political parties. While the list contributes to strengthening political life within our parties, with beneficial effects on their cohesion and programmatic construction, it also facilitates campaign expenditure oversight.

Instead of personalized accounting, under the responsibility of each candidate taken individually, we will have a single account that centralizes the expenses of all candidates from the same party. At the same time, we believe that a closed list with public financing will reduce the costs of election campaigns, which are increasingly irrational due to the great uncertainty surrounding individual campaigns.

On the other hand, our electoral process can also be improved through other specific initiatives in electoral rules. First, the end of the re-election of the President of the Republic, State Governors, and Mayors, an institution introduced in June 1997 and which, since then, has increased the power resources of elected officials, to the detriment of the principle of equality of conditions that should guide electoral disputes.

At the same time, the long duration in office, allowed by the re-election institution, has contributed to the misuse of public machinery, especially in regions and states where civil society is less organized.
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES

Similarly, we understand that the choice of all
representatives of the people can be centralized in
a single election, held every 5 years. Thus, instead
of interrupting the legislative process and the greater
difficulty for the proper functioning of the federal
and state public administration due to the restrictions
defined by electoral law, we would have the simultaneous
renewal of all representatives of the people.
At the same time, the elected officials would have 5
years to implement the proposals defended during the
election campaigns, without losing continuity of work
due to periodic elections every 2 years.
Finally, I believe we should establish in our legisla-
tion the obligation of "verticalization" of alliances,
which should be organized in the states in a manner
consistent with the agreements made in the construction
of presidential slates. This measure has two main purposes:
first, to contribute to the strengthening of the program-
matic and ideological basis of political parties, avoid-
ing opportunist alliances that, due to the peculiarities
of our electoral system, allow state government candidates
to ally with parties competing in different slates in the
presidential elections; second, together with the end of
alliances in proportional elections - a measure that will
strengthen the larger parties - this would provide the
elected President of the Republic greater ease in constru-
ing his parliamentary base in the National Congress, even
if his party, alone, has not achieved a majority of seats
in Parliament.
In summary, Ladies and Gentlemen Deputies, society
is demanding from Parliament the changes necessary
for our political system to be consistently prepared
to accommodate the social, political, and economic
advances the country has experienced in recent years.
Thank you very much.
MR. FERNANDO MARRONI (PT-RS. Without revision
of the speaker) - Mr. President, I would like to highlight
an important announcement by the Minister of Science
and Technology, Aloizio Mercadante, regarding the con-
struction of research ships so that Brazil can finally
map its 4.5 million square kilometers of territorial sea.
These ships will be built in Brazil and will be sponsored
by PETROBRAS and Vale. With this, Brazil will also be
able to conduct its own research and use these ships in
Oceanography courses in our country. Thank you very much.
STATEMENT DELIVERED BY THE SPEAKER

Mr. President, Ladies and Gentlemen Deputies, everyone who has been following us for decades, Brazil has dreamed of self-sufficiency in oil exploration, and it was only recently that it achieved this important milestone for the country's development through the discovery of oil in the pre-salt layer. This was made possible thanks to the valorization of PETROBRAS and the entire Brazilian research and innovation industry promoted by the Federal Government over the last decade.

However, one last significant barrier remains: detailed knowledge of the entire Brazilian continental shelf. But this obstacle is expected to be overcome soon. Yesterday, Science and Technology Minister Aloizio Mercadante announced, during a meeting with representatives of the Navy in Rio de Janeiro, that Brazil will make the construction of research ships in new shipyards dedicated to mapping its territorial sea and exclusive economic zone a top naval priority.

The Science and Technology Ministry wants to know in detail and as soon as possible the 4.5 million square kilometers of Brazilian territory located on the continental shelf, in order to identify economic potential, understand biodiversity, and study the effects of climate change and marine pollution on Brazil. This mapping is still in the planning phase, but the goal is for these ships, to be built with the highest technology in Brazilian shipyards, to also serve as a knowledge source for oceanography schools, ensuring an increasing number of specialized researchers.

Look, gentlemen, at how important this can be for Brazil's future. As Minister Mercadante rightly said, it is one of the last strategic frontiers that the nation still needs to fully master technically. It is a challenge as great as the one we are overcoming today by expanding our knowledge of the Amazon rainforest to preserve the wealth it offers us, both economically and environmentally.

These modern ships and the entire project to map the Brazilian continental shelf will be funded by ANP, interested in knowing the country's oil fields, and by PETROBRAS and Vale companies, which have economic interests in the continental shelf.

I believe this news is of extreme importance for Brazil, as a country can only truly understand its full potential when it invests in research and innovation, especially in strategic areas such as territorial sea and exclusive economic zone.
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES

I am absolutely certain that the investment the country will make in continental platform mapping will greatly aid us in seeing all the hidden Brazilian potential under the waters, and also serve as a basis to point out paths capable of guiding fundamental research on climate change and its impacts in Brazil.

Thank you very much, Mr. President!

Mr. CHICO LOPES (Bloc/PcdoB-CE. Without revision of the speaker) - Mr. President, ladies and gentlemen, as a citizen, a consumer advocate, and a Federal Deputy representing the state of Ceará, I come here to make an appeal to the regulatory agency ANATEL, which oversees fixed and mobile telephony, regarding what is happening in Ceará, particularly in Fortaleza.

Last week, the phones of the operator Tim did not work. The offices and sales agencies for phone devices, when approached to discuss the issue, simply ignored us. I took the device to a repair shop, and there was nothing to fix. It was discovered that they had sold more devices and lines than their operational capacity.

The State Program for Consumer Protection and Defense of the Ministry Public, through Dr. Gomes Câmara, filed a lawsuit against the operator, and the sale of devices and lines was suspended.

This week, the press in Fortaleza reported that Tim continues to sell devices and, consequently, lines. It is impossible to make a call. When a call is established, it drops. You think it is a defect and redial. And so goes the company in Ceará, without much concern.

I want to make an appeal for the regulatory agency to intervene with this operator in Ceará, because consumers deserve respect. This service is not free; it is paid for and it is expensive. Therefore, we deserve respect.

I make this appeal, otherwise, the consumer advocates of this country and of Ceará will protest in a much more forceful manner than my protest from this podium. This is a disrespect!

It is necessary for someone from the government to start looking at this regulatory agency, at the role it plays for the Brazilian people.

Thank you very much, Mr. President.

During Mr. Chico Lopes' speech, Mr. Luiz Couto, in accordance with § 2 of Article 18 of the Internal Regulation, leaves the presidential chair, which is taken over by Mr. Ságuas Moraes, in accordance with § 2 of Article 18 of the Internal Regulation.

THE PRESIDENT (Ságuas Moraes) – I grant the floor to the next speaker inscribed for Brief Communications: Deputy Luiz Couto, from the PT of Paraíba. The hon. member has 5 minutes.

DEPUTY LUIZ COUTO (PT-PB. Without revision by the speaker.) – Mr. President, Ladies and Gentlemen Deputies, yesterday we had a hearing not only to deepen our knowledge about autism, but also to disseminate that knowledge, because there is a lot of ignorance regarding what happens to families of autistic individuals, to those who have children or daughters with autism.

It is fundamental that Brazil be able to invest in research, to assist doctors, nurses, social assistants, psychologists, psychiatrists, and educators so that they can actually work with this segment.

We also have a PEC (Constitutional Amendment Proposal) coming from the Senate that benefits people with disabilities.

We know that the statute approved by this House, in two rounds, and now with aspects as a Constitution item, is not being applied by various sectors. That is why it is important for us...

It was a beautiful public hearing celebrating June 18 of this year, considered the Autistic Pride Day.

Mr. President, I would like to talk about another issue. I am very concerned about the increase in corruption in our country. We are seeing mayors being arrested. And now it's a double: arrest the mayor and his wife, also involved in activities of diverting money that should go to school meals, to health, to education. And these resources are being diverted.

In my state, Deputy Romero Rodrigues, the Federal Police carried out the called Operation Gasparzinho, which identified that a group of businessmen set up a scheme to withdraw money from municipalities. They created ghost companies and put "limes" (informal term for "middlemen") as owners of these companies. In 3 years, there was a circulation of over 23 million reais, that is, money was diverted.

This is very serious. Therefore, Mr. President, it is important for us to approve the PEC 422, from 2005, of our authorship, which deals with the creation of specialized courts for the trial of improbity crimes - I would say, for the crimes of thievery - committed by those who think they can be in the public service to steal, to divert money. We want these people to be actually condemned and barred from any bidding in public organs.

In this regard, we consider that there is a need to face the issue of corruption, because it is the driving force behind money laundering;
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES

It is through this mechanism that extortion is practiced by segments; it is through this that the payment for the largest industry in the country, the bribe industry, is made; it is through this that frauds are channeled and people believe they are in control of public power and can divert resources.

We want to congratulate the Federal Police, the General Control of the Union, and the Federal Public Ministry, who are conducting a lifting work. It has been more than 3 years of investigation! It is important to carry out this deep investigation work to catch the scheme and prevent these companies from continuing to participate in tenders. These companies should be eliminated. And there should be a national registry to state: these companies are prohibited from participating in tenders in any municipal, state, or federal public body.

If we do not do this, what happens? They are prohibited in a particular municipality or state, but they continue to participate in tenders in other states. Creating a phantom company, in the name of straw men, is a crime, and these companies will no longer be able to participate in any tender.

In this sense, we will deepen the effective fight against corruption, which is the driving force behind the diversion of public resources in our country.

Thank you, Mr. President.

MR. ROMERO RODRIGUES (PSDB-PB. Without revision of the speaker.) - Mr. President, Ladies and Gentlemen Parliamentarians, in a few words, because time is quite limited, and differently from what we usually do when we occupy this tribune to make complaints, claims, or speak about some proposals, I want to mention the commendable initiative of São Braz Industry. Its headquarters are in the city of Campina Grande. Conducted brilliantly by the renowned entrepreneur José Carlos da Silva Júnior, it recently initiated, using the space of municipal schools in the city, a campaign encouraging tree planting.

It brought, exactly in the month when we celebrate World Environment Day, the idea and the conception of the need for each one of us to encourage tree planting as a form of environmental preservation, to provide the city with more greenery, but above all, in our opinion, to try to sow in the minds of children, students of municipal schools, the conception of planting, conserving, and preserving the environment.

Therefore, I praise the initiative of this industry. At the same time, I recognize the brilliant work accomplished, including the good relationship between the servants and the institutions. It is a respectful work.

ethical and worthy of this renowned company that produces
the delicious São Braz coffee, a well-known brand at the national level.
I would like to take this opportunity to mention
that there is a bill currently under discussion in Congress that aims
to establish the mandatory planting of trees in each municipality
as a benefit of the Minha Casa, Minha Vida (My House, My Life) program. It establishes,
in accordance with the rules defined by the master plan of each Brazilian city,
for each new residential complex of the Minha Casa, Minha Vida program
and according to the system I mentioned earlier, the planting of trees.
This is due to the understanding that it is important
to conserve, preserve, and care for the environment, making every public space in the cities greener,
more conducive to the conditions necessary for a more sustainable environmental balance.
The initiative of this industry in Campina Grande
can even be copied by other companies in the city. There are spaces that need to be occupied
in Campina Grande itself, such as the Bodocongó Reservoir, whose revitalization is becoming increasingly necessary.
The reservoir is a city postcard, particularly linked to the southern area of the city, a space already sung and described in verse and prose in a song sung by Paraibana Elba Ramalho. This song,
Bodocongó, became a symbol at that time, widely known and well-regarded at the national level.
Thus, other industries in the city can take advantage of this initiative of the São Braz industry
and adopt, for example, the very Bodocongó Reservoir to start a campaign for the preservation and revitalization of that public space.
Thank you, Mr. President. That's all. May everyone be with God and have a good Saint John's Day, of course, for all of Brazil.

Ms. Íris de Araújo (PMDB-GO. Without revision of the speaker.) – Mr. President, Ladies and Gentlemen Deputies, it is my duty from this podium to reinforce our immense concern over one of the issues that most worries the population of Goiás and that, without a doubt, reveals one of the most poignant dramas since the restoration of democracy in the country: the disappearance of people after police contact in my state, which constitutes one of the most intriguing cases in our recent history.

I would like, in this regard, to share the concerns already expressed here and issue a strong warning to the authorities. This is a new underworld that has emerged in the country in recent years, in the midst of the consolidation of the democratic process, which is undoubtedly
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES

It will reveal the existence of a parallel police power,
acting in defiance of the law and instituting an unacceptable
tribunal with the power to take the lives of defenseless citizens.
Brazil needs to know what happened to 37 people who disappeared in Goiás shortly after a police encounter! Where are they? Who is responsible for this sequence of atrocities?
A newspaper report by O Popular demonstrated that, in most cases, the Goian police neglected the cases. In four situations, no inquiries were even initiated. Fifteen others remain stalled in police stations. Nine are simply archived, under the pretext of lack of materiality of the crimes. Six are being processed in court and two did not go beyond a police report.
Four months ago, a Special Commission for the Defense of Citizenship was established to investigate the cases of the disappeared. The work began shortly after the Sixth Command Operation of the Federal Police, which on February 15 of this year, arrested 19 military personnel in Goiás, suspected of belonging to extermination groups. Yesterday, this Commission presented its report, which contains new information, leads, indications and even evidence involving most of the cases.
Thus, nine archived inquiries for lack of evidence may be reopened in light of new facts.
In any case, Madam and Gentlemen Deputies, the Commission President, Delegate Adriana Accorsi, observes that it is unlikely that the bodies of the victims will be found. According to her, hundreds of people have been found dead in Goiás in the last ten years and buried as indigents. One of them may be a victim of a disappearance that occurred in Aparecida de Goiânia, a neighboring city of the Capital.
It is particularly intriguing to know that 13 of the 37 victims, after a police encounter in Goiás, did not even have a criminal record.
In this regard, Mr. President, I will forward to the Commission on Human Rights and Minorities of the House a request for an immediate visit to Goiânia to monitor the progress of the investigations and take federal measures.
The truth is that the number of disappeared since the establishment of democracy in Brazil already surpasses the dictatorial period, a reality that should indeed disturb us and lead authorities to take positions.
It is not possible that in the full vigour of the democratic regime, we have to coexist with this state of affairs, with these allegations that are emerging, without taking any action.

Therefore, as an alternate member of the Human Rights Commission, I will be present so that we can investigate and get a firsthand look at what is happening in my state of Goiás.
Enough is enough! The truth needs to come out.
That is all I had to say.
Thank you very much, Mr. President.
MR. PRESIDENT (Ságuas Moraes) - Thank you, Deputy Iris de Araújo.
MR. PRESIDENT (Ságuas Moraes) - The next speaker on Brief Statements is Deputy Teresa Surita, from the PMDB of Roraima.
MRS. TERESA SURITA (PMDB-RR. Without revision of the speaker.) - Mr. President, ladies and gentlemen, I come to this podium to present a document that I delivered yesterday to Minister of Health, Alexandre Padilha, to propose the creation of the National Network for Attention and Support for Chemical Dependents and their Families.
Crack is producing an epidemic in the public health of this country. It destroys lives, corrupts youth, and disrupts families.
According to recent press reports - and today we have this issue as an editorial in Folha de S.Paulo - there are at least 1 million crack addicts in Brazil. Twenty years ago, crack use was limited to São Paulo. Today, the drug is present in 98% of Brazilian municipalities, due to the ease of obtaining it and its low price - a rock costs between 5 and 10 reais.
Crack addicts young people from all socio-economic classes. According to experts, in many cases, it takes just one contact with the drug to create dependency.
A recent study, conducted by Psychologist Maria de Fátima Padin, from the Federal University of São Paulo, which interviewed 500 family members of addicts and ex-addicts in São Paulo, mainly from classes A and B, reveals that, on average, parents took 2 and a half years to seek some type of help. Reasons for the delay: they didn't know what to do (30%); they thought they could solve the problem at home (24%); they thought drug use would be temporary (17%). Thirty-four percent initially turned to self-help groups and churches, and 11% asked for help from a psychiatrist.
We cannot underestimate this violent and devastating enemy, but we should not be intimidated either.
We need to provide answers.
And I believe the answer is the creation of an integrated network for the treatment of dependents, where hospitalization and rehabilitation will be carried out.
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES

Its resocialization will be supported by family assistance and a prevention program.
It is essential that we have, for the treatment of the dependent, the participation of specialized professionals. We know the importance of therapeutic communities that work in conjunction with state, municipal governments, and university hospitals, but it is also insufficient, given the magnitude of the tragedy, to leave this structure, as well as the SUS network, with the responsibility of fighting this so powerful enemy and freeing our young people and their families from its grip.
I propose the creation of the National Network for Attention and Support to Chemical Dependents and their Families. This network would coordinate and integrate therapeutic communities, consolidating an assistance protocol, as well as have the physical structure to accommodate dependents in a detoxification process and subsequent technical professional qualification.
In my view, this network is a concrete response in a scenario where there are numerous good general proposals, which, although they signal good will, do not represent a solution that integrates, to guide and support society in its search for immediate solutions to the immense threat posed by the state.
I see the National Network for Attention and Support to Chemical Dependents and their Families as the materialization of the synergy between health and education areas in a single institution.
We must believe that we can take young people away from drugs, trust in the capacity of families and society, recognize successful initiatives. But it is essential that the state assume its role with vigor.
The network should implement a prevention program through educational campaigns and the training of instructors and teachers, who, through institutional contact with dependents and their families, will have concrete references to produce content that reflects the reality in which they live.
Through this continuous exchange of knowledge between health and education professionals, it will be possible to create support and training programs for dependents, ensuring, in a therapeutic and respectful environment, the conditions for them to overcome the power of drugs.
Why a network? Because the current public network's treatment structure lacks the necessary conditions to deal with the dependent. It is a challenge that requires new weapons, more resources, and urgency. We cannot hide the sun with a sieve; we cannot postpone, we cannot delegate. We need to act.

that we all, society and the State, assume our responsibility.
Thank you very much.
THE PRESIDENT (Ságuas Moraes) - Depute-
tive Teresa Surita, your proposal should be forwarded by this House to the Federal Government, so that we can effectively resolve the problem of drug users, chemical dependents, who should be viewed as a public health problem.
I congratulate you on your speech and associate myself with your proposal.
DOCUMENT REFERENCED BY THE SPEAKER
Action Plan for a Network of Care and Support for Chemical Dependents and Their Families
Actions to combat or reduce the consumption and trade of illicit drugs, particularly crack, in Brazil should consider four distinct audiences:
- the dependent
- the dependent's family
- society
- the State
- the trafficker
For each of these groups, there are different impacts and levels of responsibility and action.
For the dependent, assistance and resocialization are essential; the trafficker must be repressed and fought against.
The State also has the responsibility, in addition to implementing assistance and prevention policies, to combat trafficking. It is the State's competence to detain the trafficker.
The Network for Care and Support for Chemical Dependents and Their Families is the materialization of all prevention, care and resocialization actions for the dependent through a concrete partnership between the State, society and the families of the dependent.
In 2010, an Integrated Plan to Confront Crack and Other Drugs was launched. It is a plan of intentions, not a model of action that effectively integrates policies and initiatives in education and health.
The Integrated Plan to Confront Crack and Other Drugs, launched in 2010 by the Lula Government, establishes guidelines and presents intentions, such as the capacitation of community leaders, teachers and other civil society agents as multipliers of information about the risks of drug use and its power of dependency. It also aims to expand the care of Psychosocial Assistance Centers (CAPS), from the Ministry of Health, to treat dependents.
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES

MR. MANOEL JUNIOR (PMDB-PB. Without revision of the speaker.) – Mr. President, I thank you very much for the mention. It is an honor for me to represent in this House my native land, Pedras de Fogo, and my State, Paraíba.

And it is in the name of the population of my State, ladies and gentlemen Members, that I come to this podium to, in a perplexed manner, bring to the knowledge of Brazil, and especially the inhabitants of Paraíba, what has been happening over the past few weeks, an administrative act never imagined by anyone who cares or intends to care for public assets.

The great journalist Rubens Nóbrega, in an article of his column on June 21, 2011, makes a concise record and analysis of an administrative act that has not yet been consummated, but is on the verge of being so: the exchange of an already consolidated area for another.

Imagine, Ms. Deputy Rosane Ferreira, that the Committee on Urban Development has been dealing with municipal issues and the unwavering defense of public goods. Imagine, curiously, that the Governor of the State of Paraíba intends to exchange the area in Mangabeira, the largest neighborhood of our city, where the State Police Academy is located, a 9-hectare area valued at 135 million reais, for another totally open area in Geisel, measuring 4.5 hectares and valued at 13 million reais.

The exchange, Mr. President, leaves us at a minimum in perplexity – to say nothing of it being yet another scandal. You, Deputy Paulo Piau, another unwavering defender of public goods, understand what I am saying. It is about this administrative act that the columnist Rubens Nóbrega speaks. He questions how a property, a 9-hectare area that belongs to the State, that belongs to the people of Paraíba, and that is valued at 135 million reais, can be exchanged for another of 4.5 hectares, where nothing is built, located in another neighborhood, and valued at 13 million reais, or roughly 10% of the value of the area that already belongs to the State.

Probably, behind all this, is the same thing we have seen happen recently in João Pessoa: the City Hall expropriated an area for environmental preservation that, in any case, already belonged to public assets – environmental preservation areas belong to everyone –, for 10 million and 800 thousand reais, and just 22 days later, the value had already been paid. It was the fastest expropriation payment I have ever heard of in the history of Brazilian public life. And the worst of all was that the same actors were involved, because the order for the expropriation of the Fazenda Cuiá was given by the current Governor of the State, who depended on it.
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES

And now, the expropriation of the Cuiá Farm
serves as motivation for this exchange of an area
of the State of Paraíba's heritage for an area of
devastation—there is nothing on this land. The exchange
will simply be made because some entrepreneur—
I don't know the details—has committed to building
a new Police Academy.
Well, the Police Academy of the State of Paraíba
is one of the best in Brazil. Military personnel from

I would like to take advantage of the time allotted to me to speak about another issue that has been a significant topic of discussion, without any position taken by the government.

To whom does history belong? History has no owner, history belongs to society. We cannot rewrite history, nor impose our particular perspective on it. Yet, that is what we are witnessing at the Ministry of Education, which has used textbooks to convey to hundreds of thousands of public school students a gross distortion of recent historical events.

The book "Integrated History and Life" distributed by MEC to hundreds of thousands of children, who, in good faith, go to school seeking education - to receive education, one must be informed - is not providing them with an objective and republican narrative of recent events, but rather a packaged version of petist ideology about a supposed father of the poor, the benevolent Lula da Silva, who stands in contrast to a caricatured figure of Fernando Henrique Cardoso.

This is a gross, grotesque distortion of history, which the Minister of Education and the Dilma Rousseff government are maintaining, resisting to correct, even after the reactions from experts, educators, and Parliamentarians who spoke in this House and in the Federal Senate. It is a view from those who consider themselves above facts and truth, who want to impose their version of history on the country.

This is what we will return to address shortly, when speaking on behalf of the Minority: the issue of document secrecy, those who wish to hide history to maintain their version of the facts, without recognizing that no one has that right.

History belongs to the population. Knowing historical facts is fundamental to prevent tragedies, acts of corruption, aggression, or disrespect for human rights from repeating.

Thank you very much.

Mr. Reguffe (PDT-DF. No revision by the speaker.) - Mr. President, Ladies and Gentlemen Parliamentarians, I return to this podium to defend a bill of my authorship that exempts medicines from taxes.

In this country, 35.7% of the price of a medicine is made up of taxes. There are families that spend over 2,000 reais per month on continuous use medicines. It is absurd and unacceptable to charge the amount of taxes currently levied on a medicine. In countries like England, Canada, and Colombia, no taxes are paid on medicines. In the United States, 6.3% tax is levied on a medicine, and in Brazil, 35.7%.

I made an information request to the Ministry of Finance, from which I received a response regarding the impact of this exemption on the Budget, which would be 3 billion reais per year. Well, the Union Budget is 2.73 trillion reais. The only thing that would happen is a reduction in the Union Budget from 2.73 trillion to 2.70 trillion - that is, a reduction of 3 billion reais. The impact would be minimal on the Union Budget (0.11%), and the state would make a direct contribution to improving the health of many people in this country.

In my opinion, Mr. President, if a person has a disease, it is the state's responsibility to help them and facilitate access to the medicines they need.

I have also made a recommendation to the Ministry of Finance to implement price controls and medicine pricing tables. The free market applies to various sectors of the economy, but not to those that affect people's lives, their health. No one can live or die and have their income as the defining factor. That is not fair! That is not right!

I am also requesting a hearing with the Minister of Health, because I believe this should be a public policy: in addition to providing medicines for those with diabetes and hypertension, the government should also distribute continuous use medicines to those with other types of diseases. That is the state's role, its duty, that cannot act as if it were not its responsibility, as if this were not its problem. It is a problem, yes, of the state.

I return to say: when a person has a disease, it is the state's responsibility to help them and facilitate their access to the medicines they need.

Mr. President, I hope this House - and here I appeal to my colleagues - approves the project. It would be a significant step forward.

This Parliament's contribution to the lives of so many in the country.
We have an abusive tax burden, and taxing 35.7%
of the price of a medicine, in my opinion, is a true extortion. No one buys
medicine because they want to, no one gets sick because they want to.
The impact of this on the Budget is minuscule, I repeat,
only 0.11% of the Budget; 3 billion, according to
official information from the Ministry of Finance in response to a request
for information that I sent to that body. Three billion in a Budget of 2.73
trillion, and many in the country would benefit.
It is unacceptable that a family has to pay
over 2,000 reais per month for continuous use medicines. This is unacceptable,
especially knowing that 35.7% of the price of the medicine is tax.
Taxes can be levied on other things - cigarettes, drinks, superfluous
consumptions - but not on medicines, not regarding
the health and life of people.
Thank you, Mr. President.

Mr. President, yesterday, at the Political Reform Commission, Dep. Rosane Ferreira, who is part of that Commission, and other women in this House spoke almost unanimously, demanding that in the report on political reform, gender alternation in political representation at all levels of Parliament in this country be ensured. DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES

In the Federal Congress, only 8.7% of parliamentarians are women. On average, there is 9% female representation in all spheres of the Legislative Power in Brazil. This is lower than the participation of women in Arab countries.

Some say that there is no burqa in Brazil, and I say that there are burqas, the invisible burqas. Some say there is no guillotine, but there is a guillotine. The guillotine that decapitated feminist women during the French Revolution continues to exist invisibly in Brazil. We are in the shameful position of the second-to-last country in the Americas - we are above only Haiti and Belize - in terms of women's participation in Parliament.

We need to build a true democracy, and true democracy will only exist if we have political equality between men and women.

That is why yesterday we officially launched the manifesto of women in this House demanding gender alternation. For every man elected, a woman should be elected, so that we can truly build democracy.

Mr. President, this is a completely structuring discussion, because the more women there are in lawmaking, in budget construction, in oversight of public policies, the more we will deconstruct the subalternity enacted in this country with regard to women themselves.

Enough patrimonialism! Enough of indices like the ones we have here, in the Federal District, for example, of almost two - Deputy Rosane, almost two! - rapes per day, this year. There is a completely direct relationship between the participation of women in all spaces of power and the deconstruction of a relationship of domestic violence, which often does not even leave a mark on the skin, but leaves, in a very deep, indelible way, a mark on the soul.

That is why we, women in this House, the Parliamentarians, have signed a manifesto so that in the discussion of political reform, we can say that we are truly building democracy in this country, ensuring the equal participation of women in all spaces of power.

I conclude with the words of the former President of Chile: "When a woman enters politics, the woman changes; when many women enter politics, politics changes."

MRS. MARA GABRILLI (PSDB-SP. Without review
of the speaker.) – Mr. President, yesterday was World
ALS Awareness Day, a disease known as amyotrophic
lateral sclerosis, or ALS, which is most commonly
diagnosed in people aged 40 and above. ALS is a motor
neuron disease, the most common one – just like ALS,
there are several others: dystrophies, amyotrophies.
Yesterday, June 21st, was the summer solstice, when the
Sun is at its highest position, well north of the Equator.
This is a day of change, and it was chosen, not by
chance, to commemorate the fight against ALS.
Here in Brazil, 2,500 people are affected by the
disease each year, without a cure as of yet.
For example, I have a paralysis from the neck
down due to a car accident, and each day I fight for
more life, unlike those with a degenerative disease
who each day fight against death.
Today, I also submitted a bill that advances in
the treatment of these diseases.
There is a very interesting example, that of Stephen
Hawking, a researcher who was diagnosed with ALS in
1964. He remains alive and productive, but he is an
exception, because generally, when this disease is
diagnosed, the person has 3 to 5 years to live. When
it manifests in its most severe form, it is 6 months.
These people need certain treatments and equip-
ment that we were able to include in a 2001 decree
from then-Minister José Serra, which was amended in
2008, when it was expanded. I would like to thank the
Minister of Health and his Institutional Relations
Advisor, Edson Oliveira, for receiving us with all the
attention, allowing us to expand this decree and include
more things, such as volumetric ventilation and Cough
Assist. These equipment are vital not only for impro-
ving the quality of life of people with neuromuscular
diseases, but also for bringing significant savings to
the Treasury by preventing these people from needing
to be hospitalized in the ICU.
The personal impact of this disease is very great,
but the socio-economic impact is also immense. We
need to care not only for those with neuromuscular
diseases, but also for their families and caregivers,
who are just as affected as the patients.
I would like to say that I have a friend, Leide
Moreira, who has this disease and today is no longer
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES

She smiles with the muscles of her face. But I know she smiles
with her heart and her words. Leide Moreira is a poet
and writes with the only eye movement she has.
I will read a very short poem of hers:
“On my life's path
There is a great crossroads
No return, only going
Followed by a long road
No flowering tree
No singing bird
Only the emotion felt
That will be revealed.”
Those with ALS should not walk alone.
Everything that exists and lives needs to be cared for
to continue to exist and live, and it is this care that we
will offer to Brazilians with neuromuscular diseases,
improving their quality of life and that of their families.
Thank you very much. (Applause.)

Mr. President, Ladies and Gentlemen Deputies, I stand before this podium to comment on the Agricultural and Livestock Plan 2011/2012 (PAP), launched on June 17th in Ribeirão Preto, São Paulo. I highlight the importance it holds for the country and for the Brazilian agricultural and livestock sector.

Rural producers will have more resources to finance the next harvest, which begins in July. The Federal Government has allocated R$107.2 billion to finance agricultural production in the 2011/2012 season. This value is 7.2% higher than that allocated in the 2010/2011 cycle.

The plan was announced by President Dilma Rousseff and Minister of Agriculture Wagner Rossi. I would like to point out that among the plan's novelties are specific financing lines for livestock that will enable the purchase of breeding stock and reproducers, and resources for the renewal and expansion of sugarcane plantations.

These guarantees are important in order to offer better conditions for the producer to continue expanding agricultural production, always with a focus on sustainability. The Government's estimate is that with this volume of resources, a grain harvest of 170 million tons can be achieved.

The reduction of interest rates on credit lines offered to rural producers and the expansion of resources offered to the sector are significant. The interest rates are accessible and compatible with the condition of a competitive agricultural policy.

Livestock breeders will be able to contract up to R$750,000 for investments in the purchase of bovine and buffalo reproducers and breeding stock. In the 2011/2012 season, the livestock breeder will also have a cost coverage limit 136% higher than that established in the previous plan. The value will increase to R$650,000, covering beef, dairy, ovine and caprine, beekeeping, and pig farming. Last year, the limit was R$275,000.

Thus, it will be possible to concretize more food, more income for the farmer, and environmental preservation.

I would like to emphasize that another innovation of the Agricultural and Livestock Plan 2011/2012 is the unification and increase of the financing limits for cost coverage of all cultures and activities to R$650,000 per producer. The change represents an increase of up to 225% in the maximum amounts that can be contracted. Previously, each product had a set limit.

The Secretary of Agricultural Policy, José Carlos Vaz, states that the Government's intention is to stimulate the diversification of agricultural activity, benefiting equally commodity producers, focused on export, and producers who supply the domestic market. A total of R$80.2 billion will be allocated to

THE PRESIDENT (Ságuas Moraes) – I grant the floor to the Honorable Deputy Antonio Carlos Mendes Thame for a Leadership Statement by the Minority, for 6 minutes.

MR. ANTONIO CARLOS MENDES THAME (PSDB-SP. As Leader. No speaker review.) – Mr. President, Ladies and Gentlemen Deputies, the concept of “eternal secrecy” for official documents has been the subject of severe and well-founded criticism from the public.

The National Association of Newspapers (ANJ) stated in a note that Brazil needs a law guaranteeing citizens’ right to access public information and allowing the country to know its own history. The National Federation of Journalists (FENAJ), the Association of Federal Judges of Brazil (AJUFE), and the Brazilian Bar Association (OAB) also share this understanding.

According to the President of AJUFE, the Association of Federal Judges, Dr. Gabriel Wedy, the Brazilian citizen has the right to know the history of his country. He noted that our Constitution stipulates that “the public power has the obligation to make its acts public,” and emphasized that over 90 countries already have legislation regulating access to public information.

In 2009, the bill addressing public access to information was sent to the National Congress by then-President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.

Last year, the Chamber of Deputies approved an amendment to the text, limiting the renewal of the secrecy period for ultra-secret documents. It limited the renewal to only once. Thus – 25 years was the limit, plus 25 years – 50 years would be the maximum time for a document to remain under secrecy. The bill, approved by the Chamber, was sent to the Senate.

There was an expectation of swift processing and approval in the Senate. However, the Leader of the Government in the Senate, Senator Romero Jucá (PMDB/RR), announced the removal of the project’s urgency status, allowing for a longer period of analysis – much longer – increasing the risk of it not being approved this year.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs classified 426 documents as ultra-secret last year. Under the current law, these documents can remain under secrecy indefinitely, with the mere extension of their classification as ultra-secret documents every 25 years.

They join millions of official records, such as those related to the War of Paraguay, which ended 141 years ago. To this day, all documents remain secret.

The argument that disclosure of these historical documents could reignite controversies and cause embarrassment with neighboring countries is unfounded. It is an argument that conceals other interests.
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES

ses, that have nothing to do with the interests of a diplomatic or peacekeeping nature in our external relations with neighboring and bordering countries.
The Attorney General of the Republic, Roberto Gurgel, states that any barrier against the right of all to public information is unconstitutional. He also says that he will appeal to the Supreme Court if the Senate maintains the secrecy of these historical documents.
In a recent article written for the newspaper Folha de S.Paulo, Gregory Michener, an expert in transparency and a Ph.D. in Political Science from the University of Texas in Austin, stated that "the changes advocated by two former presidents and current senators have no precedent in the democratic transparency standards advocated by the United Nations and the Organization of American States."
The fact is that the President of the Republic, Dilma Rousseff, is adrift. She says something different every hour. Initially, she supported the text approved by the Chamber. She then spoke with these two senators, former presidents, and became in favor of eternal secrecy. Subsequently, the lucid, always lucid, current Minister of Foreign Affairs, Antonio Patriota, declared that there is no secret document that causes discomfort to Itamaraty. None of them. He made a thorough search and stated that the government can disclose such documents, as none of them causes discomfort to anyone.
But the President of the Republic changed her mind again. She announced that she would stop interfering, that she would follow the guidance of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and let the project follow its normal course, that is, already approved by the Chamber, whose text does not provide for the eternal custody of the documents.
However, today she changes her mind again. The newspaper O Estado de S. Paulo states that President Dilma is once again in favor of eternal secrecy for the documents. The question remains: who benefits from this defense of eternal secrecy? What is it that causes this topic to provoke so many changes in the position of the President of the Republic?
After all, we all know that history is the work of men, and men are not eternal. Nor are nations. Just look at the map of Europe to see how it has changed and how nations, after the fall of the Berlin Wall, have changed.
History is the record made of the present to ensure the indispensable evolution to the perfectioning of coexistence among men and the progress of relations between peoples.
Mistakes and successes are part of the trajectory of men. Often, mistakes are much more useful for the evolutionary construction of human action. To do this, we need to know them, know these mistakes.

Lastly, the secrecy of official documents cannot be left to the discretion of public officials. Nowhere does the law state that public officials are owners of these documents. These documents belong to the nation. The right to memory is common to all, without belonging to anyone in particular.

Disclosing documents that, for state reasons, have become classified prevents the perpetuation of atrocities. They need to be disclosed at some point. They mitigate the face of authoritarian regimes. Omitting and concealing is the practice of spurious governments. We cannot acquiesce to this trend of the petist government to have a penchant for the pact of silence. This has been the case with the "aloprados," with the "mensalão," with the consultancy of former Minister Palocci. It is the shortest path to darkness. With this, we cannot agree.

Thank you, Mr. President.

Speaks the following speech.) – Mr. President, Ladies and Gentlemen Deputies, I take to this podium at this moment to denounce the Government's decision to make the budgets and expenditures for the 2014 World Cup and 2016 Olympic works secret.

Ladies and Gentlemen Deputies, once the budgets for the works are kept entirely secret, values can be negotiated at a hefty bargain and at the price of gold, as in practice, the contractors will set the final price of the undertaking, and since the initial values are secret, they will not need to justify any potential overruns. We will open the door for favored contractors to be free from any conduct rules and have access to the data.

A world of utopia will be projected if it is not discerned that there is a frightening gap for promoting the dark side of corruption. Millions of reais will flow through the sports games' works, and this should be rigorously overseen by the Public Ministry. It is notorious and public knowledge that even with the rigor of the Law of Tenders, some 2014 World Cup works are already budgeted at astronomical values, causing astonishment and losses to the Brazilians.

Bill No. 1,359, of 2011, which contains proposals to improve the financing
of drug control policies. The Bill aims to enhance the funding for the National
Anti-Drug Fund, established by Law 7,560 of December 1986. The proposal provides
for the possibility of deducting donations made in favor of Drug Control
Policy Funds from Income Tax.
This is a right that every taxpayer has,
to be able to determine the destination and portion of their Income Tax to
pay, through direct donations to certain funds that promote social policies.
To increase the amount of resources available
to the management committees of these funds, it is of fundamental importance
to make it easier for taxpayers to direct their donations. This undoubtedly
gives these funds more dynamism, enabling, for instance, a significant increase
in the amount to be invested in drug prevention and control policies.
The possibility for taxpayers to decide how
a portion of their Income Tax will be applied means, without a doubt, a victory
in building responsible and solidary citizenship. This is the great merit of
the incentive in question.
In this context, the experience with other
funds that already have similar mechanisms has been crucial in refining this
legislation. It is therefore necessary to universalize the effective participation
of Income Tax payers in social actions in favor of drug user attention.
To do so, it is essential to simplify legal,
administrative, and operational procedures to make this benefit easier for
taxpayers to use, also introducing measures aimed at improving corresponding
fiscal controls.
Thus, this bill, of my initiative, among other
actions, provides for the simplification of procedures currently in place.
Currently, only a small portion of donations are made through this mechanism.
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES

A portion of taxpayers has been exercising their citizenship by allocating part of their taxes to various funds aimed at expanding resources for social policies. Excessive bureaucracy has been an enemy of citizen participation in financing social policies. The proposal also extends the deadline to benefit both legal and natural persons, with the aim of allowing the taxpayer to decide, at the time of the annual adjustment, the exact amount they wish to allocate to drug policy funds.

Unfortunately, existing legislation discourages many taxpayers from making donations. This is because the incentive is a percentage of the tax due, and consequently, while this number is not determined, the taxpayer must subject themselves to a series of uncertainties regarding the deductible amount. This bureaucracy ends up being an obstacle to the inflow of significant resources for the implementation of drug control policies.

My proposal also establishes the simplification of operational procedures related to in-kind donations by providing for the possibility of the taxpayer using a special bank deposit model containing all the necessary information to prove the donation to the Federal Revenue Secretariat.

Another provision of the bill requires that information about donations be provided annually by the bodies responsible for administering the accounts of the National, State, District, and Municipal Drug Policy Funds to the Federal Revenue Secretariat.

I have actively participated in this House in all discussions related to the drug theme. I am a member of the Parliamentary Fronts to Combat Crack and to Defend Therapeutic Communities and also part of the Special Commission on Public Policies to Combat Drugs.

Like several Parliamentarians, I have chosen this theme as one of the priorities of my mandate because I understand that Brazil needs to address the drug problem urgently, taking broad and consistent measures in three fronts: prevention, treatment, and social reinsertion of chemical dependents, and repression of drug trafficking.

We are making progress in the debate around solutions in these three areas and want to offer the country a solid contribution, with a view to improving our legislation and public policies to combat drugs.

The Federal Government has also demonstrated that the fight against drugs is a priority issue, where some important measures are already being taken.

We have noticed across Brazil that several states and municipalities are beginning to mobilize around this issue.

issue, adopting actions to face the complexity of this topic.
I am certain that, in this struggle, it is of extreme relevance that, alongside the formulation of public policies, there is a political will to increase the resources to be applied in these actions.
The true priority given to addressing a problem can be measured by the allocation of funds for initiatives aimed at overcoming it.
In the case of drugs, we need to find alternative paths to expand the amount of resources to be invested in public policies in this sector. It was precisely thinking about this that I presented the Project of Law No. 1,359, of 2011.
I thus hope to contribute my part to this battle that knows no party or ideology. It is a battle of all of us, of all Brazilian society. Together, we will be able to face this new challenge, restoring hope and the will to move forward to thousands of Brazilian families.
That was all I had to say.

I grant the floor to the first speaker of the Small Order, Deputy Sebastião Bala Rocha of the PDT from Amapá.
MR. SEBASTIÃO BALA ROCHA (PDT-AP. Without the speaker’s review.) – Mr. President, ladies and gentlemen, next Friday, April 24, I will accompany members of the Legislative Assembly of my state on a trip to Oiapoque to address cross-border issues of interest to Amapá and French Guiana.
I hope that cooperation between Brazil and France will become increasingly productive for the development of the region. Mr. President, there are many problems there, primarily illegal mining and the irregular entry of Brazilians into the territory of French Guiana. This situation will only be reversed when Brazil and France join forces and structure a development project for Oiapoque. We have been working towards this goal.
I am the author of a bill to create a free trade area in Oiapoque, a clear demand of that people, so that in the near future, new initiatives can emerge in the economic sector, as the gold economy is declining, given the strong repression carried out by the French government against illegal mining in French Guiana. We therefore need economic alternatives, and one of them is the free trade area.
There are others, such as fishing and transforming Oiapoque into a university city. We need to invest in knowledge and implement a knowledge-based economy in the Oiapoque region.
The bridge connecting Brazil to French Guiana has already been built; only a few structures are missing for its inauguration, such as a border post.
Therefore, Mr. President, I hope that this event next Friday, sponsored by the Foreign Relations Commission of the Legislative Assembly of Amapá, will be a success for the development of Oiapoque.

STATEMENT BY THE SPEAKER
Mr. President, Ladies and Gentlemen, I would like to register my condolences and solidarity with the family of driver José Góes dos Santos, who was assassinated this week in my Belo Horizonte.
This solidarity extends to his work colleagues, who are on strike in protest against the violence they face on a daily basis.
The suspension of activities caused a true chaos this morning in Venda Nova, particularly at the BHbus station in the region, which serves 60,000 passengers daily. Venda Nova is one of the two districts of Belo Horizonte – the other is Barreiro – but like Barreiro, it has become part of the city and has an estimated population of over 300 people. There is not a single day that we do not come across a scene, a news report, or an image of extreme violence decimating workers, students, families, and fracturing social bonds.
In Venda Nova, the assassination of José Góes dos Santos, while driving a collective bus on Line 640, from the Jardim Leblon neighborhood, was for a trivial reason. Two fugitives got on the bus and asked the driver to stop in a location other than the designated stop by the transport company and the city's Traffic Department. The driver refused, as he could be fined and lose his job, since the bus is monitored. That was enough for them to shoot him.

Against him, who was taken to the hospital Risolta Neves in the region, but did not withstand his injuries.
Angry, and with reason, as they lost another companion in a barbaric manner, the drivers halted their activities. Many public transport users, who need the bus to go to work, school, in short, to move around, do not understand the movement, as they are also drastically affected and indignant by the losses suffered. The spirits are high and there are even records of physical aggression attempts between the parties.
Ladies and gentlemen, we need to rethink our relationships of coexistence, public security, the upbringing of our children. One of the assassins is only 14 years old; the other, 19 years old. We cannot coexist with children and young people without any parameters of fraternity, civility. We cannot be exposed to robberies, shots and deaths even inside buses. We can no longer flex our patience. We can no longer turn a blind eye to the chaos installed. Not even!
During Mrs. Jô Moraes' speech, Mr. Luiz Couto, § 2nd of Article 18 of the Internal Regulation, leaves the Presidency chair, which is occupied by Mr. Sebastião Bala Rocha, § 2nd of Article 18 of the Internal Regulation.

MR. LUIZ COUTO (PT-PB. Without the speaker's review.) - Mr. President, Ladies and Gentlemen Deputies, it is important that we be able to approve the project that deals with the Truth and Memory Commission and, I would say, also with justice. We consider it important that the documentation that is still under secrecy be given public exposure.
We want to congratulate President Dilma, who, even under pressure, considered it important to publish these documents, especially those in which human rights violations are present, so that the Brazilian population becomes aware of what happened during the dictatorship period and learns the lesson. And that something like that never happens again, as it occurred during that period when democratic freedoms were abolished.
So, in this regard, we consider it important to continue the debate. No one wants revenge. We want the Brazilian population to know what happened, become aware of the facts, and for those responsible for those atrocities to at least ask for forgiveness.

Apologies to the Brazilian Nation for the torture, the disappearance and death of many people.
I congratulate the Government on its position. The truth must come out, because the truth sets us free.
