MR. MARLLOS SAMPAIO (PMDB-PI. Without revision by the speaker.) - Mr. President, Ladies and Gentlemen Deputies, I am here to make public an important hearing that I had yesterday with the Minister of Human Rights, Federal Deputy Maria do Rosário, when we once again addressed the problem of loan scams against our elderly, against a population that today numbers around 20 million Brazilians.
We request that the National Conference on the Rights of the Elderly, to be held in November, include the problem of loan consignations in its agenda for discussion. It is necessary to call FEBRABAN to participate in these meetings, so that we can reach a consensus and, together, united with the Secretariat of Human Rights, the Ministry of Social Security and FEBRABAN, make a national advertising campaign feasible to alert the elderly about the traps that can be set by unscrupulous people who use loan consignations to illegally enrich themselves.
This has already been adequately proven in a dossier that we presented to the Commission on Public Security and the Fight against Organized Crime, at a large public hearing held last week, which was very productive and served to show this House, to the Brazilians and Brazilianas, that today, loan consignations generate more than 100 billion reais in the Brazilian economy. More than 40 million contracts have circulated since last year until now.
So, these are stratospheric numbers that generate a great concern. They are astronomical numbers, far superior to what I imagined. We need to focus on this concern and make the issue public. May this House take the necessary measures, may other Deputies join this noble cause in favor of retired people in Brazil.
THE PRESIDENT (Sebastião Bala Rocha) - Thank you very much, Mr. Deputy Marllos, for your participation.

THE PRESIDENT (Sebastião Bala Rocha)
– I invite the Deputy Fernando Marroni, from the PT of Rio Grande do Sul, to speak.
Mr. President, Ladies and Gentlemen Parliamentarians, Brazilians watching on TV Chamber, last Friday, President Dilma Rousseff and Agriculture Minister Wagner Rossi launched the 2011-2012 Crop Plan.
First of all, I would like to highlight the 107.2 billion reais that will be offered in credits for agriculture. A record, if I may say so.
However, in this statement, I would like to refer to the Low Carbon Agriculture Program, ABC. Created in 2010, the new investments in ABC, announced by Dilma and Rossi during the Crop Plan launch ceremony, show that sustainable agriculture has become one of the main axes of the Brazilian Agricultural and Livestock Plan. ABC will incorporate all investment programs aimed at efficient production with sustainability. Thus, it will have an investment of 3.15 billion reais in the new Crop Plan. That is, noble colleagues, 3.15 billion reais.
From now on, ABC will encompass the Commercial Planting and Forest Recovery Program – PROPFLORA and the Program to Stimulate Sustainable Agro-Livestock Production – PRODUSA. According to Minister Rossi, “the government is taking large steps to make Brazilian agriculture and livestock one of the most innovative in the world”. Among the new ABC actions, there is direct planting on straw, degraded areas recovery, crop-livestock-forest integration, commercial forest planting, biological nitrogen fixation and animal waste treatment.
And all this, ladies and gentlemen Members of Parliament, will be within the reach of the producer, as access to credit will be easier. The ABC Program interest rate is 5.5% per year, the lowest fixed for rural credit intended for business agriculture. The repayment period can reach 15 years. Producers and cooperatives can contract up to 1 million per beneficiary.
However, the Brazilian Government's concern goes beyond Low Carbon Agriculture. President Dilma announced that she will also expand the crop financing limit, fixed at 650,000 reais, for producers who adopt sustainable practices such as direct planting on straw, organic farming system and those who already have or present a plan for recovery of permanent preservation areas (APPs) and legal reserve. This value can be expanded up to 45%, depending on the number of techniques used by the producer.
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES

Therefore, I would like to extend my sincere congratulations to all involved in this great initiative of the Federal Government. Our country is already a reference when it comes to sustainable development, and actions such as the Low Carbon Agriculture Program reinforce this image. We are a green country, from the Green Harvest. I conclude this statement with a phrase from President Dilma that encapsulates the Federal Government's thinking on this topic: "Efficiency will only come if agriculture is hand-in-hand with sustainability."

Thank you, Mr. President.

THE PRESIDENT (Sebastião Bala Rocha): Thank you, Sir. Congratulations on the speech you just made from this House's podium.

THE PRESIDENT (Sebastião Bala Rocha): Deputy Gonzaga Patriota has requested the floor for one minute. Sir, you have the floor.

DEPUTY GONZAGA PATRIOTA (Block/PSB-PE. Without revision by the speaker): Mr. President, just to register the departure of our beloved President of the Republic, Dilma Rousseff, to Caruaru today, which is very important.

I see Leader Luiz Couto from Paraíba, where they also have the São João de Campina Grande, near Caruaru. But the President has chosen to go to Caruaru today, and obviously she will go to Paraíba later. This is important for the Northeast.

In a moment, I will speak in the Grand Committee about the Northeast. I thank our President for going to Pernambuco and also to Paraíba. Certainly, the President will address something from the "Treaty of Tordesillas" that I will bring up in a moment.

Thank you.

THE PRESIDENT (Sebastião Bala Rocha): Continuing with the Small Committee, I grant the floor to the distinguished Deputy Luiz Couto, in exchange with Deputy Jô Moraes.

DEPUTY LUIZ COUTO (PT-PB. In order. Without revision by the speaker): Mr. President, Ladies and Gentlemen Deputies, first of all, I would like to thank Deputy Jô Moraes for the exchange.

Mr. President, we need to make a permanent fight against the violence practiced against children, adolescents, and women.

Today, Bom Dia Brasil (Good Morning Brazil) disclosed an alarming figure: every day, women are being murdered, even with the Maria da Penha Law. This reveals that violence is locked in the heart, mind, and entrails of those who do not realize that that person, that woman, the image and likeness of God, should be respected, loved, and not have her life taken.

People who do not have the dignity to respect the human being.
This violence is strengthened and fed by another factor: impunity. People commit crimes, violate women, rape women, kill children, execute young people and adolescents and are not punished. Just check that in almost all states there are so-called mysterious crimes. There is a victim, but there is no perpetrator. Why? Because often the investigation itself is not carried out. Families are afraid to denounce. Sometimes, when they denounce, the police chief says: "It's better not to give a statement here, because it might get complicated, your husband is violent, so it's better for you to stay calm, because later he might act more violently." This happens, unfortunately.

Moreover, the state itself, through the forces of some segments of the police, which perpetrates the violence, needs to put an end to this violence scheme, which is great in our country.

Mr. President, until April, in São Paulo, there were seven massacres committed. In most cases, young people were eliminated.

The worst thing, Deputy Jô Moraes, is that these young people, according to the police itself, had no criminal record, no police entry; neither a complaint or a term was issued against these people.

This shows that it is violence practiced by criminal organizations that make money killing for the pleasure of killing, executing. Sometimes because the young person made a joke with someone, he must be killed; or because the young person, at a party, argued with someone, he must be killed. What kind of talk is this? Is there no respect for human beings?

In this regard, we need to put an end to this violence. It will only have an effective fight when we also face corruption, which is where it strengthens; bribes, extortion and impunity.

Deputy Jô Moraes, in her speech, speaks of a worker who was executed. We can no longer accept that people are summarily executed, which brings suffering to the family and to all those associated with that person.

It is necessary to put an end to it. That's what we all want.

Mr. President, there is a bill from my initiative, PL nº 370/2007, which has been pending approval for a long time but always encounters resistance.

It is the bill that typifies the crime of genocide. This crime is a violation of human rights.

If this bill is approved, the investigation, denunciation and trial of these crimes will pass to the Union sphere. Also, these crimes will be considered against the democratic state of law.

And the punishment as well. If the crime is committed by a
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES

The public manager or public servant, he has his sentence increased.
The project was already on the agenda for voting, but
we learned that there is pressure from segments to prevent its approval. We do hope, however, that it will be put back on the agenda and that we can put an end to this criminality practiced by extermination groups, death squads, and pistolery.
Thank you very much, Mr. President, for the additional time you have granted me.
MR. PRESIDENT (Sebastião Bala Rocha) - Deputy Luiz Couto, the desk supports your statement. It highlights that you are one of the most dedicated Deputies to the cause of human rights here in the Chamber of Deputies, and for that reason, we also express our concern regarding the issue brought to the floor by you, both as regards urban violence and rural violence.
Unfortunately, we still have to coexist with these plagues in today's Brazil. Do you need to supplement your speech, Deputy?
MR. LUIZ COUTO - Thank you very much. Just to thank you for the references.
MR. PRESIDENT (Sebastião Bala Rocha) - Thank you, Deputy Luiz Couto.
MR. PRESIDENT (Sebastião Bala Rocha) - It is with pleasure that I invite to the floor, in order, the Deputy from Minas Gerais, Jô Moraes, from the PCdoB Bloc. You will have up to 5 minutes.
MS. JÔ MORAES (PCdoB Bloc/MG. In order. Without revision by the speaker.) - Thank you very much, Mr. President, Deputy Sebastião Bala Rocha.
We are at this moment in the House discussing the Law of Budgetary Guidelines. And what is the importance of this debate? It is that we must, when approving this law, define the priorities that we will have for the budget to be considered at the end of the year.
And among these priorities, we must have a comprehension, not of the small problems of each state, of each city, but of the major problems that plague our country. Brazilians is a solid, meritorious, and necessary achievement that must be pursued daily. There is no doubt that since its implementation, consecrated in the 1988 Constitution, the SUS (National Health System) has improved significantly, and access to health has extended to almost all Brazilian citizens and foreigners present in our country, but it is still far from fulfilling the constitutional precept of providing quality care to all. We can witness this deficiency of the SUS in long waiting lines, prolonged, inefficient, and incomplete outpatient care, delays or impediments in elective surgeries, and limitations or absence of authorization for requested examinations.

We need to urgently address these issues, as delays in healthcare are life-threatening. To improve healthcare, we must first change the care model. It has long been established that one of the problems with the current model is that healthcare service delivery is concentrated in the hospital system, leading to higher costs and resolution only for the most severe or acute cases.

To achieve better coordination of services offered to the population, we must have excellent primary care to coordinate the entire network.

Hospitals, AMEs (Local Health Centers), UPAs (Urgent Care Centers), and other services should be regionalized and articulated, operating in a rationalized manner, focusing on prevention and promotion of chronic disease health.

Healthcare financing should have sufficient resources per capita per year to provide comprehensive care to all, and these resources should be allocated based on international averages. In this quantification, we should consider, for comparative purposes, even the costs of complementary healthcare, such as those practiced by UNIMEDs, which are a reference in this sector.

This cost, or the money needed to provide the constitutionally mandated care, is currently around 4,500 reais per capita per year, a value far from the 750 reais per capita per year that the SUS currently applies.

Health Minister Alexandre Padilha has spoken extensively about the need for better management, and we agree with him. We must professionalize management, incorporate modern management tools, avoid duplication of efforts, define what "health expenditures" are (which we will achieve with the regulation of Constitutional Amendment #29), redefine the sectoral federal pact, innovate in structures, and introduce economies of scale.

The interest of physicians in specialties with greater social impact has been decreasing due to several factors,
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES

Among these, the lack of conditions to perform their work, low salaries, and the absence of a state career for the profession. We need to find ways to encourage young doctors to specialize in family health, pediatrics, general practice, and geriatrics.

Pharmacies need to be health promotion agents and not mere business counters. This will be achieved by valuing the pharmacist, a professional underutilized in these establishments.

Let's fight for the SUS (National Health System) dream of quality and accessibility to become a reality for all. The money is limited, but it is possible to do more and better with what we have. A resource complement, even temporarily small, that corrects the SUS table and allows, at a minimum, cost coverage is necessary and immediate.

The SUS is not a problem without a solution, but rather the solution to the health problems of the Brazilian people. That's it.

Thank you very much, Mr. President.

MR. JOSÉ STÉDILE (Bloc/PSB-RS. As Leader. Without the speaker's revision.) - Mr. President, Ladies and Gentlemen, I promise to try to be brief so as to share the space with our Deputy Gonzaga Patriota, so that he has enough time to make his statements.
The current electoral model is deeply unfair, as it privileges those with more resources and gives large parties a huge advantage in the distribution of existing seats. Changes are necessary, but we must be careful not to make the current situation even worse.
Look at the example I am describing. If a certain party gets 720,000 votes and another gets 150,000 votes, and ten seats are up for grabs, the party A, which got 720,000 votes, will elect nine Deputies, while party B, which got 150,000 votes, will only have one Deputy.
This is the distorted way the current legislation benefits large parties. This calculation model needs to be changed, regardless of political reform, so that the will of the population that voted is respected.
Two aspects that are little debated in the political reform hearings concern me. The first is the unfair distribution of seats. And the second is the end of the possibility of alliances in proportional representation.
I conducted a study, Members of Congress, in all Brazilian states to assess, if there had been no alliance in the 2010 election, what the current composition of Federal Deputies in the Chamber would be.

In the National Congress. If there had been no coalitions, or the possibility of coalitions, in 2010, the Workers' Party would have had 25 additional Deputies; the PMDB, 31; and six parties that are currently part of this House would have ceased to exist. That is why I believe that often the PT and PMDB come here to advocate for the end of coalitions. Well, they will grow; 26 and 31 Deputies would have been part of the base of these two parties if there had been no coalition. This is the logic of transferring, of concentrating in a few parties. This happens in an election; in the next one, the difference will be even greater. In a short time, we would have in Brazil two, three, or four parties, at most, because the small and medium-sized ones would be extinct. In addition to these parties, practically all the others would lose Deputies. My party, the PSB, for example, currently has 34 Deputies, and would have 29, losing 5; the DEM would lose 7 Deputies. I calculated, state by state, what the new reality would be if there had been no coalition. I am denouncing this because there is strong discussion in this House about the possibility of ending the coalition. If the end of the coalition comes with the end of the electoral coefficient, it will be possible to analyze. But I highly doubt that will happen.

Therefore, I ask all parties that are not from the PMDB or PT to pay attention, because this will, in the short and medium term, be the end of the small and medium-sized parties in this House.

I also want to register, Mr. President, Ladies and Gentlemen Deputies, President Dilma's concern for the poorest. She is just, she is correct, she is consistent, but there is a great distortion between what she proposes and what the Federal Savings Bank, through a normative act, has been doing regarding the "My House, My Life" program. President Dilma proposes that the more poor people who have homes, the better. However, the normative act of the Federal Savings Bank states that in order to build homes under the "My House, My Life" program, there must be asphalt paving or any other type of paving.

The problem is that many streets in several Brazilian municipalities are not paved, and the municipalities do not have the conditions to pave them. Therefore, exactly the most impoverished class of the cities is being excluded from this program, because the municipality cannot pave the streets, nor can the owner pave their own street.

I also want to register that we are receiving today the distinguished visit of the Mayor of Cachoeirinha, Vicente Pires, who was called by President Dilma to participate in a meeting regarding the treatment of chemical dependents in the country.

The festival envisages an ecumenical celebration, a walk, the presentation of a manifesto for agrarian reform, drafted by the Goian Forum for Agrarian Reform and Field Justice, cultural presentations, the unveiling of a monument marking 25 years of the conquest of the Mosquito and São João do Bugre settlements, and traditional forro.
We take it upon ourselves to record this event and recognize that much has already been achieved, but we also emphasize that much still needs to be done. Agrarian reform continues to be a necessity for workers and workers who have historically had their right to land denied. No one is landless by choice. Just in Goiás, there are over 10,000 people living in camps. We consider that (more than for the campistas) agrarian reform is a benefit for everyone. With agrarian reform, only those who historically gained – the latifundistas – lose.
Agrarian reform generates employment, income, local development, healthy food, and reduces population in cities. It can be an ally of the environment, which the latifundio, with its productive processes, has always destroyed. If the Constitution guarantees the social function of land, it should be expropriated for agrarian reform purposes when it does not fulfill its role, as provided by the Federal Constitution.
Official data from INCRA (as of January 2011) shows that the area incorporated into the agrarian reform program increased from 21.1 million hectares of land obtained between 1995 and 2002 to 48.3 million, between 2003 and 2010. The number of families benefiting from the program also increased over the last 8 years, reaching the current 614,093. During the same period, 3,551 settlements were created. Currently, Brazil has 85.8 million hectares incorporated into agrarian reform, 8,763 settlements served by INCRA, where 924,263 families live.
These numbers have their relevance, but it is a fact that our historical delay requires that we advance even further. Our parliamentary mandate is an ally of the Government of President Dilma, in actions aimed at expanding access to land, with technical assistance, and investments in family farming, which sustains over 70% of Brazilian families.
We stand ready to strengthen and support the great mobilizations of workers, such as the Grito da Terra Brasil, the March of the Margaritas, and the struggle for agrarian reform, for sustainable agroindustries and livestock farming in the Center-West and Brazil. Our side is that of rural workers, small producers, family farmers, and rural wage earners.

STATEMENT SUBMITTED BY THE SPEAKER

THE NORTH EAST, ITS CHALLENGES AND THE SOLUTIONS

Mr. President, Ladies and Gentlemen, this afternoon I want to bring to the Brazilian people a picture of the Northeast region of Brazil, and I do so with the permission of the 154 Ladies and Gentlemen Deputies from this prosperous and suffering region.

Two months ago, I took on the coordination of the Northeast parliamentary group in this House of the National Congress. Since then, I have met several times with the coordinators of the state parliamentary groups in the Northeast, and without any surprise, I found that all the states in this region face the same challenges as the people of Pernambuco, starting with the lack of a macro-policy of government investments to take it out of the headlines as a region that tarnishes the country's image, particularly in comparison to the developed countries of the planet.

The Northeasterners served very well in building the Brazilian Southeast, particularly São Paulo and Minas Gerais.

In the 18th and 19th centuries, Rio de Janeiro, and in the middle of the 20th century, Brasília, the Capital of the Republic, served as collateral for large loans with so-called First World countries, contracted by governments that passed through Brazil, especially during colonial and exceptional periods, in the dictatorships of Vargas and the coup-making generals from 1964 to 1985.

After Brazil's democratization at the end of the last century, students, housewives, blacks, Indians, minorities, workers of all categories, among other social classes, began to organize into Associations, Unions, NGOs, Cooperatives, and other associative means, and took up a significant space in Brazil's democratic process, particularly in politics.

Who, before the democratic process, saw a black, an Indian, a family farmer worker, or a bricklayer, including few women and only with family and political tradition in the Legislative Houses, in the State Governments, and in the Presidency of the Republic, as has been occurring since the promulgation of Ulysses Guimarães' Citizen Charter?

We went through the fragile and timid government of President José Sarney, then the chaos of Collor de Mello's government, 2 years of the also slow government of Itamar Franco, until the 1992 elections, when Brazil elected Fernando Henrique Cardoso, who began to govern looking at the country as a whole and not just the South and Southeast of Brazil.

No one can deny that the social programs implemented in Brazil during President FHC's government were the beginning of the process of liberation of the Northeastern people, especially when he managed to hold onto President Itamar Franco's Real Plan, stabilizing our currency and helping investments in that region.

With Brazil's democratization, its independent people elected a Northeastern worker as President of the Republic, companion Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, in the 2002 elections.

Lula was a different President from all who passed through Brazil, in several aspects. First because he prepared to govern the country, walking through all its regions. He went to the South, saw the riches of the papas. In the Southeast, the industries transforming the products produced in its rich and fertile lands, well cared for.

The Central-West, which was also very poor, Lula had already seen its development, mainly through the construction of the Republic's Capital, Brasília, in this region, which attracted many products and industries, particularly to the states of Goiás and Mato Grosso.

From the South. He visited the abandoned North and its Northeast,
from tip to toe.
The 8 years of President Lula's government, with
its important social programs and the opening of
easy credit, primarily for the middle and lower-
middle class, included a significant portion of Brazilians
who lived below the poverty line, facts recognized

I recently read an interview of a Chilean researcher
stating that, to the former president FHC's dismay,
it was inevitable to admit that contemporary Brazil
is divided into "before Lula and after Lula," and
mentioned the profound transformations the country
underwent from 2003 onwards, notably an unprecedented
fight against poverty. Another foreign observer,
British historian Perry Anderson, in a lengthy article
recently published in the London Review of Books,
titled "Lula's Brazil," contextualizes the successes of
the ex-president's management, his commitment
to improving the living conditions of our people,
reminding the difficult situation the country faced
when the petist took office, and also shows that,
during the 8 years of Tucan management, the public
debt had doubled, the current account deficit was
twice the Latin American average, the SELIC rate
was above 20%, and the Real had lost half its value.
Besides being explosively unequal, Brazil in 2003
was also a broken country.
It is important that observers from all walks of life
recognize the advances Brazil has made in recent
years. But it is a much greater cause for satisfaction
for us socialists who supported Lula, as we now
support Dilma, to know that the Brazilian people
widely approved this project and bet on its contin-
uity.
For me, who is from the Northeast, from the state
of Pernambuco where ex-president Lula was born,
these transformations have a special taste and
meaning. I will mention one: in 2008, Lula and
Eduardo Campos, Governor of the state of Pernambuco,
celebrated, at the Palace of Princesses, the achievement
of 100% electrification in that state. It is important
to remember that rural electrification was one of
the priorities of the last government of Miguel Arraes,
Eduardo's grandfather, who launched in 1987 the
"Light in the Field" program. To bring electricity
to the poor rural population without charging for
installation is to put into practice a commitment
to justice and socialist principles. It is the change
from the candle to the light bulb, the possibility
of preserving food in a refrigerator, of operating
a sewing machine or an irrigation pump, of lighting
a child's crib.

At the time of Arraes, many people reacted to that use of public resources, probably the same ones who had shudders when seeing Bolsa Família beneficiaries acquire their first stove, their first refrigerator. Indeed, I saw the opposition propose an amendment, during the voting of Provisional Measure No. 517, which extinguished the extension of the General Reserve of Reversal, one of the financing sources of the Luz para Todos program, which is transforming the lives of so many Brazilians. So far, over 13 million people have been benefited, and the investments reached R$19 billion.

I spoke of electricity, now I will speak of water. We all coexist today with the growing threat of water scarcity, globally. According to the World Bank, the number of people without access to potable water, this essential resource, has tripled since 1950, reaching over 1 billion human beings today. It is estimated that around 2027, due to demographic expansion, degradation of water resources, and uncontrolled industrial and agricultural expansion, no less than one-third of humanity will suffer from water scarcity. This scarcity, according to experts, will be felt more acutely in arid and semi-arid regions, coastal areas, and the metropolises of developing countries.

In this context, the whole world is beginning to turn to our Country and its extraordinary water resources, its rivers and watersheds. And I would like to mention a successful Northeastern experience, a program established by a modest action of this also modest Deputy, the Programa Água para Todos (Water for All Program), drafted by City Councilor Pedro Norberto from Petrolina in 2005 and already implemented in Bahia by Governor Jaques Wagner the following year.

This ambitious program was created with the objective of increasing water supply and expanding sanitation services, helping to eradicate poverty. While other governors did not believe in the Programa Água para Todos, the state government installed over 100,000 cisterns, approximately 2,000 tubular wells, and over 1,500 simplified supply systems throughout Bahia, prioritizing the semi-arid region, the São Francisco watershed, and the main urban and rural centers. For example, riverbank populations, people covered by Bolsa Família, residents in the periphery of large centers, settlers of agrarian reform, and remnants of quilombos were benefited. With an investment of approximately 2 billion reais, the program has already brought water to over 2 million people and sanitation to almost 1 million.

The São Francisco micro-region, in total, has seven municipalities: Afrânio, Cabrobó, Dormentes, Lagoa Grande, Orocó, Santa Maria da Boa Vista, and Petrolina, which hosted the event. The agreements were for water supply and sanitation works in Petrolina, totaling R$94.5 million. After Petrolina, it was Araripina's turn to host the "Todos por Pernambuco" seminar, which brought together 915 people and 299 entities from the 10 municipalities that make up the Araripe Plateau. The population of this region had the opportunity to voice their aspirations and discuss priority actions in seven thematic rooms (education and culture, health, security, social development, infrastructure, economic development, and sustainability, as well as a free theme) and during the plenary session. The Araripina seminar took place at the Araripe Technology Center from 8 a.m. to 7:30 p.m.

Governor Eduardo Campos opened the afternoon activities, authorizing the theme room secretaries to present a summary of all the proposals discussed. In addition to the secretaries, three representatives from each theme could also present their claims to the public. One of them was farmer Maria Enertina de Jesus, known as D. Lia, who had the opportunity to speak about the problems in her community. "I will be able to take all the knowledge I acquired here to my farmers' association. Here at Todos por Pernambuco, we have gained even more confidence in the government," she stated.

In a press conference, Governor Campos reminded that the Todos por Pernambuco seminar was also a way to translate the government's program into the population and ensure that the themes presented are debated. "The Todos por Pernambuco model is not that of a deliberative forum. It aims to bring up issues and make sure the discussion is collective, forming a debate in which entities prioritize what is most important for the region. Following this, as was the case in 2007, we will define in the PPA (Multi-Annual Plan) what will actually be done, according to the main aspirations of the population," he clarified. He also reminded that all the commitments made by the government at the first seminar had been fulfilled.

Several proposals were put forward. The main ones were family farming, the construction of cultural centers, the implementation of UPAs (Urgency and Emergency Care Units), and road construction. Sister Fátima, who works in the health sector in Araripina, proposed changes to the health model in the municipality and praised the choice of the new secretary for the sector, Antônio Figueira. "In the room, we had direct contact with the secretary, and I concluded that you (Eduardo Campos) chose very well. He is firm and will do a lot," she said.

The Araripe micro-region comprises the municipalities of Ipubí, Bodocó, Exu, Moreilândia, Granito, Ouricuri, Trindade, Santa Filomena, Santa Cruz, and Araripina. All these cities were represented.

Minutes later, Governor Eduardo Campos arrived at the venue and visited the rooms, met with the press, and in the afternoon chaired the plenary session, where Lucas Avelino da Silva, just 11 years old, made a request: "I want to learn to read and write." Blind since birth, Lucas is a resident of the rural area of Cedro and shared his story of perseverance and dedication with the governor.

Just as Lucas, Mr. President, other voices were heard during these three days of seminars. Petrolina, Araripina, and Salgueiro together brought together 2,329 people from 694 entities. This direct dialogue with the population, where the governor, the vice-governor, and all the secretaries actively participate in the discussions, is viewed positively by all. Now our struggle is to get the construction of the military village. Whenever identifying in its project a way to accelerate the development process of women, SecMulher, in addition to meeting the immediate needs of women, imprimes to its action a long-term perspective, aiming to transcend the emergency character of the Straw Hat.

Every year the Network is expanded in its territory of action, covering in 2009 a total of 53 municipalities and 7 municipalities of the São Francisco Valley, not only increasing the number of women attended by the Straw Hat Woman, but also offering professionalizing courses.

In the same year, it also extends to 17 municipalities of lower IDH in Pernambuco and the municipality of Arcoverde.

Thus, combining characteristics of meeting the practical and immediate needs of the population with strategies of transforming the disadvantageous conditions of gender, race and ethnicity of women, the Formation of the Network of Public Policy Agents for Rural Women builds a logic that opposes the reproduction of women's subordination condition, offering them the chance, through the offer of knowledge, group dynamics and meeting practices, to design their social and economic autonomy. Such logic allows, immediately, to constitute in a public action structuring social and economic changes in people's lives, with corrective impact on the unequal relations experienced in the state of Pernambuco.

The structure of action development

The work program of the Network of Public Policy Agents for Rural Women starts with the realization of opening seminars, consisting in an inaugural lecture, in which the focus and the theme to be adopted in the following courses are established.

The second step is the realization of workshops for unifying gender concepts for educators and recreators, followed by the execution of the Public Policy Course and the Professionalizing Courses.

Finally, the work is finalized with the Closing Seminar, with the participation of most of the women who participated in the courses. During the training period, workshops for monitoring and evaluating the work done are also held, aiming to correct possible deviations, renew themes related to women's empowerment and indicate new ways of acting for the formulation of courses in the following year.

The logistics also involves the idea of care. Women, being from the rural area, often live far from the Municipality's centers. This reality, frequently, makes their participation in any type of training unfeasible. Thinking about this, the Secretariat of Woman decentralizes the classes, bringing them closer to the rural women.

Women's activities, such as providing transportation assistance and recreational facilities, have been implemented. The project includes recreational activities where, while mothers participate, their children up to 7 years old play and learn in a safe environment with trained recreators, demonstrating the possibility of reconciling productive and reproductive lives. Providing snacks for women and children participating in the project is also part of the care for individuals.

Another crucial element of this logistical design was the creation or strengthening of institutional networks. Hiring NGOs to conduct activities within the Straw Hat Woman Project in the Sugarcane Zone and Fruit Cultivation, as well as the Convergir Woman Action Project, which have experience in social work, knowledge of the local reality, and have acquired and enhanced knowledge on gender themes, confirms an important decision by the Women's Secretariat. The social experience of these entities has filled a gap left by the public power for decades. Through partnership with NGOs, the SecMulher aims to contribute to local development, promoting the hiring of educators and recreators in municipalities, as well as strengthening local trade and services.

Professional training courses
In 2008, a new activity modality was introduced: professional capacitation, expanded in subsequent years up to the present.

The proposal is for all women to go through the public policy module and the professional training module, possibly repeating the same module. The intention is for women to become linked to the Network as multiplier agents, encouraging their neighbors to participate in meetings, attending city association meetings, seeking educators to assist them in setting up a women's association in their municipality.

The professional training module was designed with quality as a goal. A partnership was established with the S System (SENAI, SENAC, SESI), and courses were planned according to the potential of each region (tourism, handicrafts, food, civil construction, etc.). Participants receive the same course, with the same number of hours and the same certificate as anyone who completes a SENAI or SENAC course, becoming effectively competitive in the job market.

The courses are diverse: sweets and savory foods, hydraulic firefighter, gardening, electrician, handicrafts, stonecutting, housekeeping, motorcycle mechanics, car electrician, among others.

Now, dear colleagues
Members of Congress, allow me to speak a little
about the region where I have lived for almost 40 years, Petrolina and the São Francisco Valley. It produces over 1 million tons of fruit annually and employs 240,000 workers, more than soybean cultivation with its nearly 23.5 million hectares across the country. Grapevine cultivation, on just 12,000 hectares, generates 72,000 direct field jobs at the peak of the harvest. More than just simple numbers, this is a reality that cannot be overlooked. While soybean occupies an area of over 23.6 million hectares across the country to employ half of those people. It would take 48 million hectares of soybean to employ the same number of people as work in the São Francisco Valley's productive areas. To put it into perspective, the total area harvested of all of Brazil's agricultural crops in 2010 was 48.1 million hectares.
The annual revenue of the São Francisco Valley approaches 2 billion reais. The resources annually entering the country, resulting from the export of mangoes and grapes, equate to approximately R$500 million. The reflections of the movement of these resources in the other economic sectors, and their consequent social effects, are extremely relevant for the region. I highlight viticulture, as only on its 12,000 hectares are more than 72,000 direct field jobs generated during the peak of the harvest.
The grapes produced in the São Francisco Valley have a quality standard to meet the most demanding markets, anywhere in the world, thanks to the efficient control of the production system that is monitored and certified by various quality protocols, such as Tesco, Global GAP, PIF Brazil, among others.
In today's globalized world, news reaches quickly any part of the world, promoting almost instantaneous results of the reported facts. When the news is derogatory, resulting from disastrous and irresponsible research conducted by a government body, the results are terrible. I refer to the report broadcast on Globo Repórter, a program on Rede Globo, on March 25, 2011. The main topic of the program was the promotion of organic products. Without entering into the discussion of what was presented about this production system (as, in our opinion, the report was manipulated and biased, as organic products may not have chemical contamination, but they do have biological contamination of all sorts, especially with fecal coliforms, facts not disclosed), the matter

It referred to grapes as the second most contaminated product with agrochemicals in Brazil.
This news, based on research conducted by ANVISA, committed the disastrous and irresponsible error of not disclosing the origin of the products analyzed. The fact is that without knowing the origin of the problem, it is practically impossible to envision a solution.
The grapes analyzed, whose results were presented, could have been imported – and it is generally known that many imported grapes use products prohibited in Brazil, and there is no disclosure of this irregularity. Grapes could also have come from an amateur producer who does not follow technical parameters and much less production protocols, such as PIF Brazil, and there are no traceability records of the fruit, making it impossible to know if any product was applied, which product, why, and when it was applied.
In recent history, Mr. President, Brazil continues to live various forms of discrimination; whether racial, social, or homophobic. It is notorious that discrimination stems from prejudices, leading to the exclusion or stigmatization of certain segments, groups, or activities. By stating that grapes are the second most contaminated product with agrochemicals in Brazil, without revealing the origin of the fruit, the reported display prejudged all grape producers, unfairly. It was, moreover, an act of extreme cowardice, as it attacked not only the producers but an entire region of Northeast Brazil, without allowing the accused to defend themselves.
The report, without a doubt, will produce immense discrimination against grapes, potentially reverberating even in exports from the São Francisco Valley, remembering that only the São Francisco Valley exports grapes in Brazil. This discrimination against grape producers and the São Francisco Valley must be clarified and publicized to the entire Brazilian and foreign society.
ANVISA provided a service to Brazil by discriminating Northeast and the fruit cultivation of the São Francisco Valley, contributing to increase unemployment and misery in our region. The error committed by ANVISA in not disclosing the origin of the grapes analyzed, cited in the article, cannot go unpunished.
By the way, I reiterate a previous request to the directors of ANVISA, especially to its President, to pay attention to the gravity of the problem. The reported broadcast by the important television program does a disservice to the nation, as it does not explicitly state the material analyzed. Generic information such as this causes doubts and brings losses to the economy of the São Francisco Valley, in the Sertão of Pernambuco.
Someone must be held responsible for the information.

By Roberto Amaral

Former Minister of Science and Technology, Brazilian General Director of Alcântara Cyclone Space, and Vice-President of the Brazilian Socialist Party.

"The challenge of space conquest is as passionate as it is thorny, because between the indispensable dream to do it and the objective reality, inevitable, there are not a few obstacles pointing our path, which demands effort and humility to face misunderstandings and even resistances, some clear, others veiled, but both difficult to overcome.

The 'case' of ACS is characterized by the convergence of strategic interests between two countries. As everyone knows, we have, not only in Alcântara but throughout the North and Northeast regions of Brazil, the best area on the planet for rocket launches. For two very simple reasons:

(I) In the Alcântara (Maranhão) region, for example, we are at 2.2 degrees south of the Equator, while on the Ceará coast, at 3.8 degrees south (Kourou, in French Guiana, where the European launch center, the second best location, is at 5 degrees north) - this gives any object on the surface a high tangential velocity, in other words, a very favorable initial impulse for equatorial launches, as is the case with communication satellites. This translates into an increase in the carrying capacity of the launchers, making them more competitive compared to launches at higher latitudes, that is, further from the equator.

(II) Facing our coastline, we have a vast and extensive maritime area, which is essential for security purposes. Thus, launches can follow simpler, 'flat' trajectories and directly place satellites into orbit, practically without the need for maneuvers, unlike all other launch centers. For this reason, some visionaries thought that we had all the conditions to set up a large space-scientific complex. The initial idea was to have, next to the current Alcântara Launch Center (CLA), operated by the Air Force and dedicated to the VLS, three additional space launch sites capable of operating with other vehicles, in addition to those already being developed by the autonomous program. One of them would be the Cyclone-4 of ACS. And we would have, as a backup for these sites and due to them, a park of companies supporting space activities, as well as institutions for teaching and research in pure and cutting-edge technology. In addition, the technical revolution in the region would substantially favor industrial and service activities, enhancing the development of the tourist potential of the Alcântara and Ludovicense regions.

Let's remember that in 1980, the conception of the CLA provided for the implementation in a vast area of 62,000 hectares, of which only 20,000 would be used for operational purposes (the rest would be for the relocation of people, for natural reserves and for the establishment of an industrial support park). the difficulties posed to Brazilian strategic projects. Access conditions are an exemplary case.

The locations ended up being mobilized to prevent the initial field studies. (I refer to the February 2008 blockade) And as if that wasn't enough, we were not allowed to remain in the area previously ceded by the federal government.

The judge of the 5th Federal Court of Maranhão gave us 24 hours to leave, from the area previously ceded by the Brazilian state, hence the need to install ourselves within the CLA, which took several months of negotiations. In total, this operation consumed 14 months, between the blockade of our area and its release by the justice system, and we spent approximately a year negotiating with the Ministry of Defense, negotiations that were successfully concluded, allowing us to secure an area, our current 462-hectare area (the original was 1,298 hectares).

Nevertheless, we are very grateful to the Air Force, as it welcomed us in the little space it had left. It was them who saved the project, but we left an area with free access and entered an area where access is subject to military logic, norms, and rules, often incompatible with industrial projects. We are now meeting with CLA companions, because construction has finally begun, and we need to register all technicians, all employees from ACS transferred, and the workers (estimated at 1,500 during peak construction) from the contracted companies for the site construction, as well as define control systems that reconcile our access needs with the security dictates of that military center.

Looking back at the origins of the space race, we see how distinct the actions were that made the dream a reality, fulfilling the needs and strategic aspirations. Russia began its space program in 1950, Brazil in 1961. By 1988, Russia was launching reusable vehicles. The United States, which also started in the same decade, have long operated manned spacecraft and stations, in addition to a wide range of probes exploring the Solar System and deep space. The advances of these leading countries, motivated by the Cold War and their economic needs, were cumulative and spectacular. But were only these countries, along with Japan and European countries like France, the only actors on the space scene?

There are other space programs that also deserve attention. China, for example, began in 1956. And in 2003, it already sent a man into space. India has already launched satellites and probes, the same happening with Israel. South Korea, after the failure of its first launch in 2010, is on the verge of becoming the most recent country to enter the 'launchers club'.
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES

North Korea and Iran are ahead of us. Our first rocket-building activity dates back to 1965. We advanced with a family of suborbital probe vehicles. We produce and operate small and medium-sized satellites. However, our satellite launcher has not been successful, after no less than 30 years of efforts. Why? Are we incompetent, or does God not like Brazilians? The answer is simple: we are the 23rd space program investor if we consider each country's GDP. The resources allocated for investment in the Brazilian space program do not exceed 0.010% of our GDP, that is, about ten times less than France, Russia, and China.

Let's look at our situation in relation to the BRICs. Russia invested $2.44 billion in its space program in 2009, while we have only $164 million. It's still too little, but we have to admit: investments, which had been declining, were resumed at the beginning of this decade, a turnaround led by President Lula's government. When the VLS accident occurred, I gave an interview as Science and Technology Minister, stating that the VLS project had been fatally wounded by the resource diet. I was criticized by everyone, including government colleagues. In this text, I repeat that assertion, now backed by irrefutable data, namely, the resource allocation chart from 1980 to 2009 (as we know, the accident occurred in 2003) and the conclusions reached by the Parliamentary Inquiry Commission of the Chamber of Deputies, convened to investigate the causes of the accident.

Only in the period 1985-1989 did investments focus on the three activity segments - satellites, vehicles, and launch centers - with an average annual expenditure of $100 million. From then on, penury! In 1990, investments dropped to $57 million, and in 1999, they did not exceed $9.9 million. In total, the country spent only $530.2 million from 1980 to 2002 (the eve of the VLS launch) on space programs. How can we seriously think about launching our VLS if the government reduced investments every year? From $27.5 million in 1995, we dropped to $18.7 million in 96, to $11.271 million in 97, to $10.408 million in 98, and finally, to $3.7 million in 2002. In 1999, the government had the audacity to only apply $1.6 million!

This is the summary of the attention we are giving to strategic projects. In 26 years of VLS development, which would be our first satellite vehicle, we made three attempts, three failures. Was the effort in vain? Of course not, as a lot was learned and advanced. But the accident compromised the pace...

and cast doubts on various aspects of the project.
And how have we reacted? What is the critical mass of researchers, engineers, and technicians we have to learn from failures, review projects, and envision solutions? What is the actual, sustainable involvement of industry that we have achieved? The inanition to which strategic projects are subjected leads to this dragging of few results and to the abandonment of professionals and companies. See also the case of the nuclear submarine: we have been developing it for 21 years and, depending on cooperation with France, we may have to wait another decade, at least. Certainly, there is a need to rethink the way and the firmness with which strategic projects should be conducted, something that transcends governmental periods and requires decades of investment in generations of professionals, in training and research entities, in laboratory infrastructure, and in an industrial park with continuous demand.

What is the Brazil-Ukraine meeting? Ukraine has one of the best rockets in the world, but due to geographical reasons, it does not have a launch site and cannot have one because it cannot conduct launches without its rocket flying over other countries, discarding its various stages. Ukraine, therefore, is currently forced to launch its rockets from Russian and Kazakh sites, Plesetsk and Baikonur. On our part, we have excellent areas (as we have seen in previous lines) for the location of launch sites, but we do not have a rocket. This is what is called an intersection of interests. ACS is a space transport company that, in addition to meeting the direct interests of both countries, can compete, with advantages, in the rich global market for satellite transport.

The importance of satellites is obvious, but a satellite is not neutral, it is not for use only in a civil context, not only for meteorological use, it is for almost everything. Including for gathering strategic information, monitoring borders, monitoring our seas and oil platforms, guiding police and military movements, guiding tele-guided weapons, and ensuring the functioning of the new air traffic control system CNS/ATM.

The Space Program anywhere in the world is dual, which is why it is difficult for bureaucracy to understand the true challenge. The issue is not just the commercial use of our launchers, but we are already objects of satellite espionage. "If we do not have the capacity to launch our satellites, whether they be what they may, from Brazilian soil, with a Brazilian rocket, we will not be able to guarantee the sovereignty of our country."

Regarding ‘water management’, DNOCS has always done it efficiently and competently, despite the limited financial resources allocated for this specific purpose. It was, and still is, an important activity carried out by the agency, since its early existence, to put it briefly, without fanfare and propaganda. Just look at the mature and unquestionable water infrastructure that this Federal Department has implemented and has been operating since its creation in 1909, that is, for over 100 years. For those who don't know, DNOCS has the largest collection of hydrometric data (pluvimetric, evapometric and fluviometric) in Latin America.

For the reader of this Blog to assess, the state of Ceará has about 18 billion cubic meters of accumulable water in public and private dams, both at the federal and state levels. Of this total, DNOCS monitors 85%, while COGERH monitors only 15%. However, out of the 130 dams existing in the state of Ceará, DNOCS monitors 60, while COGERH monitors 70.

To achieve this goal, thanks to its administrative structure and personnel for its various activities, DNOCS provides only five employees, two of whom are engineers, while COGERH, as we have previously mentioned, has around 500 employees and is announcing a public contest for the admission of 65 more servants. This fact is important to be said, without any other purpose than to demonstrate the responsible authorities for the social and economic success of this undertaking, a claim of over 100 years from the Northeastern population, which is not advisable to create a specific company to manage it at the federal level, a mission that could be assigned to a DNOCS Directorate, without significant investments, whether in the administrative or personnel areas, including in terms of the utilization of the general physical installations and equipment of that Department in our Region.

SOCIOECONOMIC CHARACTERIZATION OF THE BAIANO WEST

The Mesoregion of the West of Bahia has a history of growth marked by economic peculiarities distinct from other regions of the state, these, combined with its natural characteristics and territorialization agents that operated therein, were responsible for the region's current identity.

Although late, the economy of the West region developed and currently has a diversified base, mainly in the agricultural sector, with a focus on grain production. The purpose of this work is to understand the Bahia territory, more specifically the studied region, in order to propose intervention actions on the problems found, as well as evaluate the main proposal currently presented by the public power: the creation of the state of Rio São Francisco, which encompasses the entire territory of the region and part of the municipalities of the Mesoregion of the Vale do Rio São Francisco. The work relied on bibliographic research and selection, as well as semi-structured interviews applied to political representatives of the municipality of Barreiras.

The Baiano West comprises the entire territory of the Mesoregion of the Extremo West and part of the municipalities of the Mesoregion of the Vale do São Francisco (regionalization established by the Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics - IBGE). In this article, the West is considered as the entire territory of the state of Bahia located on the left bank of the São Francisco River, or the delimitation previously described.

The highlighted region has peculiar physical aspects, with notable distinctions from other spaces in the state of Bahia. The most striking natural characteristics of the Baiano West are the climate, the relief, and the hydrographic network. The predominant climate is the Tropical Continental, characterized by two well-distinguished periods: a rainy one and a dry one, summer and winter.

**LOCATION OF THE BAHIA WEST REGION**

Although late (from the second half of the 20th century), the economy of the West developed, becoming the main agricultural pole of the state and currently has a diversified base. The region is part of the area for the creation of a new Federal Unit, the State of Rio São Francisco, already under evaluation by the Federal Senate. Despite achieving significant economic growth, the Bahia West region has a social reality marked by inequality and deficiency in basic existence factors, demonstrating that economic growth was not accompanied by social development.

**HISTORY OF THE TERRITORY OCCUPATION**

The history of the Bahia West occupation is marked by the importance of the São Francisco River, which was the only means of connecting the region with other spaces, and later its main tributaries, located on its left bank. Beyond São Francisco and the Gerais - as the lands on the left bank of the river and those near the borders with other states were called, respectively - were distant from the more dynamic demographic and economic network of Bahia, the state's coastline, characterized by sugar cane cultivation on fertile massapé soils. The two regions were separated by a dry and inhospitable sertão and intermittent rivers, which also hindered flow, as technical transportation networks were incipient.

In the 17th century, the first occupation initiative of the region occurred with the insertion of cattle ranching, as cattle was a self-transportable commodity. Thus, the number of settlements increased.

The economic activity of the West Baiano region, even with the greater diversification observed at the end of the 20th century and beginning of the 21st century, still relies on the primary sector. Cotton cultivation and corn production also have evidence in the economic matrix of the West region. Cotton is an activity that incorporates high technology, the region is responsible for 97% of state production and is second in national scale, in addition to possessing one of the largest cotton productive chains in Latin America. The history of the Western region demonstrates a lack of territorial identity with the State of Bahia. In the 16th century, it belonged to the Captaincy of Pernambuco, as did all lands on the left bank of the Rio São Francisco. With the end of the Hereditary Captaincies and the idea of emancipation of Pernambuco, already in the 19th century, the then Comarca of Rio São Francisco was annexed to the province of Minas Gerais, remaining for a short time. Due to administrative difficulties, the highlighted region returns to be part of Pernambuco. After a new revolutionary act by the emancipation movement, in 1824, the comarca was again administered - this time with a provisional character - by the Minas Gerais province.

Due to political disagreements between Dom Pedro I and the Minas Gerais leaders, also with a provisional character, in 1826, the Comarca of Rio São Francisco was annexed to Bahia. The first attempt at emancipation was in 1830, with the aim of transforming the then comarca into a province, but it had no impact. Other projects with the same objective emerged, but without prominence. At the end of the 20th century, in 1998, Legislative Decree Project 631/98 was presented, which gained, especially in recent times, great popularity, and has become a topic of discussion in all spheres of society.

The population of the municipalities of Barreiras, São Desidério, Angical, Baianópolis, Santa Maria da Vitória, Cristópolis, and Cotegipe mobilizes to urge the approval of the creation of the State of Rio São Francisco, a part of the State of Bahia that has a significant development in the agro-business sector and lacks public support for works to facilitate production outflow. This document presents some of the characteristics of the Municipality of Petrolina, its people, its multiple developmental actions, and also its problems.

I – Introduction

CHARACTERISTICS OF THE MUNICIPALITY

01 – Location and Accessibility

The city of Petrolina is located in the extreme west of the state of Pernambuco and is part of the homogeneous microregion of the São Francisco River's sertão.

This city has a privileged location as it is situated on the left bank of the São Francisco River, which serves as the state boundary between Pernambuco and Bahia, and is approximately equidistant from Recife (776km), Salvador (518km), Fortaleza (854km), and Teresina (665km). The main access route between Recife and Petrolina is provided by BR-232, which crosses the state from east to west, with Petrolina being intersected by BRs 122 and 428, which traverse Pernambuco from south to north, with BR 428 being the main connection between large areas of Northeast Brazil and the central-south region of the country. The Municipality has three Districts: Rajada, Izacolândia, Cristália, and Curral Queimado—the latter having been proposed to be incorporated into the settlement of Uruás. It is also worth noting that between Petrolina and Juazeiro lies one of the few bridges connecting both banks of the São Francisco River, the Presidente Dutra Bridge, which is currently being duplicated, with resources allocated, in part, through our participation. Thus, the city of Petrolina emerges as an important road hub in the state network, as it also receives BRs 407 and 235, and serves as a passage point not only for a significant portion of the commercial flows from the central-south region bound for the states of Pernambuco, Paraíba, Ceará, and Piauí, but also for exports via inland routes.

It can be stated that Petrolina's physical location, along with other economic factors, constitutes one of the main locational advantages compared to the vast majority of cities in Pernambuco.

02 – Physical-Environmental Aspects

The site where the city of Petrolina is located develops along the banks of the São Francisco River, presenting a flat topography with elevations ranging between 360 and 380 meters. Its average elevation is considerably higher than the maximum river flood level, thus not experiencing flooding problems.

Soils range from sandy to conglomeratic, with an average thickness of 2.5 meters, which can reach 5.0 meters in favorable locations. They consist of alluvia from various stages of the São Francisco River's development, with conglomerates at the base and fine sandy layers at the top. Thickness varies due to irregularity.
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES

It has a topographically irregular crystaline surface. The arboreal vegetation is sparse, with native grasses commonly found in the riverbanks of the São Francisco River. Except for the São Francisco River, the site does not present other significant geographical accidents. However, the landscape is greatly enriched by this river, with a notable volume and characteristics. The Municipality of Petrolina is located in the southeastern part of the state of Pernambuco, in relation to Arcoverde, and northwest in relation to Recife; it borders Dormentes to the north, the São Francisco River to the south, Lagoa Grande to the east, and Afrânio and the state of Bahia to the west. The municipality occupies a real area of 4,701 km², with a population of 280,000 inhabitants, of which 137,096 are men and 142,904 are women. The demographic density corresponds to 59.57% inhabitants per square kilometer. 76.2% (213,360) of the population resides in the urban area, and 23.8% (66,640) in the rural area.

**03 – Historical Formation**
In 1840, the area where Petrolina is located today was called "Passagem de Juazeiro." It was, at that time, an uninhabitated place. A simple crossing point of the São Francisco River for travelers from Ceará, Piauí, and Pernambuco, heading to Bahia and the south of the country. This passage was, therefore, a convergence point of several regional paths, and at this time, some settlements for traveler's support began to appear.

As a result, a small nucleus began to strengthen, which in 1862 was constituted as a parish and elevated to the category of village by the same Law nº 530 of June 7, 1862, with the name of Petrolina, in honor of Emperor D. Pedro II, who was then on the Brazilian throne.

Petrolina was temporarily suppressed by provincial law but was restored by Law nº 921 of May 18, 1870. Its reinstatement occurred on May 24 of the same year. It became an autonomous municipality on April 25, 1893. Law nº 130 of July 3, 1895, elevated Petrolina to the category of city, and it was installed on September 25 of the same year.

**04 – Infrastructure**
The Municipality of Petrolina stood out in the 1980s as the beginning of more intense development. In this decade, the primary and secondary sectors were intensively dynamized by public and private initiatives through the implementation of large irrigation projects by the Company for the Development of the São Francisco Valley – CODEVASF and agroindustries.

In the early part of this decade, the area under irrigation (public) was only 12,000 hectares, while the private initiative area reached 4,000 hectares. By the end of the last millennium, the irrigated area had already reached 81,959 hectares, with 36,959 hectares from public initiative and 45,000 hectares from private initiative. During this period, three large tomato processing agroindustries (unfortunately, now closed) were established.

The structure of the Semi-Arid Tropic Agropecuary Research Center - CPAT-SA, one of the decentralized units of EMBRAPA, was also consolidated.

These facts, associated with an already established infrastructure for transport, communication, and social equipment in the Municipality, contributed to an effective dynamization of the local economy, with repercussions in the tertiary sector, attracting various financial institutions to the region. The efficiency of transportation means was increased with the presence of the São Francisco Valley Airport, capable of daily landings of large aircraft; communication means (newspapers, radios, and TVs) were made viable; basic services (health, sanitation, education) have been dynamized, transforming the Municipality into a development pole with direct influence within a 300km radius.

The economic dynamism of the region, impressed by these socio-economic facts, has contributed to slowing down exodus and stimulating population attraction from other regions, not only from Pernambuco but also from neighboring states.

With a population of 280,000 inhabitants, it is the sixth largest Municipality in the state and the fifth with the highest annual growth rate, over 6%. The urbanization rate is 80%, and its population is distributed over an area of 4,701 square kilometers.

The urban zone, located on the banks of the São Francisco River, occupies an area of around 60 square kilometers, and its urban equipment follows the current master plan (unfortunately) established in 1983.

It has a service infrastructure with indicators above those of Brazilian municipalities.

05 - Sanitation
The sanitation system in the Municipality of Petrolina serves just over 60% of the population.

There are several locations where sanitation still does not exist, including: all Districts and Rural Settlements within the Municipality; as well as neighborhoods: Jardim Imperial, Portal da Cidade, Alto do Cocar, Vale do Grande Rio, Pedra Linda, Henrique Leite, Fernando Idalino, Vila Marcela, Vila Carolina (IPSEP I), Dom Avelar, Santa Luzia, and various Housing Developments.

06 – Transportation

Air
Petrolina Airport is the second largest in the state, with a runway measuring 2,100x45m, now expanded to accommodate large cargo aircraft with weekly flights carrying fruit directly to Europe. The airport offers services such as a bar, snack bar, restaurant, shops, travel agencies, a car rental service, taxis, police, fire department, and health surveillance.

Road

Internal road transportation is served by a fleet of taxis scattered throughout the city, with approximately 300 vehicles. Several bus companies, including Joalina, Vale do Sol, and Menina Morena, among others, provide passenger transportation with a fleet of approximately 150 buses. There is also a fleet of approximately 150 vehicles that provides alternative public transportation between Petrolina, Lagoa Grande, Dormentes, Afrânio, Casa Nova, and other locations, as well as urban mototaxi transportation with over 500 motorcycles, without any regulation.

There is an interstate bus terminal with various services, catering to several regional bus companies. Due to its state management and inadequate administration, the company Itapemirim and others in its group constructed a support point in another location and removed their buses from the public terminal. Because of these and other issues, the state government decided to municipalize the bus terminal.

The current governor of Pernambuco, Eduardo Campos, has invested heavily in the Industrial District of Petrolina, reactivating its administration, paving the streets, and offering incentives to those who set up there, which is now concluding the sale of the last lots for the installation of numerous industries in that industrial district.

17 – Commerce

Retail commerce in Petrolina is represented by over a thousand legally registered companies, with the textile, hardware, shoe, construction materials, and tools sectors standing out.

The wholesale commerce sector has around 200 companies, mostly in the food, agricultural inputs, cleaning supplies, and other sectors.

According to the CDL (Commercial Association) and the Association of Microentrepreneurs of Petrolina, the municipality has approximately 2,000 microenterprises, distributed between legally registered and unregistered companies, operating in the industrial and commercial sectors.

While many stores have closed their doors, particularly in the city center, informal commerce has grown alarmingly.

This is due to the rise in unemployment rates and the lack of incentives and credit from governments, which do not support small and microentrepreneurs, who opt for clandestinity, without paying taxes and without signed work contracts, as they understand it.

The region primarily produces mango (9,800 hectares), grape (8,800 hectares), sugar cane (10,500 hectares), tomato (1,500 hectares), no longer producing on a large scale due to pest attacks, particularly the whitefly, banana (4,864 hectares), acerola (5,500 hectares), asparagus (700 hectares), and others such as pine, lemon, coconut, passion fruit, guava, etc.
Irrigation has had a socio-economic impact, among other aspects, as it promoted changes in the existing technical base.
A sequeiro area, inserted into the socio-economic context of the Northeastern semi-arid region. In the economic area, the issue is the sustainability of activities. Extensive livestock farming requires an area of support that does not match the current land situation. Technology must be incorporated into this process to adapt to the new spatial reality.
In the social area, the presence of public services, family income is lower in irrigated and riverbank areas. The urban zone of Petrolina has two distinct natural areas: the center and neighborhoods.

Having made these considerations regarding the characteristics of the Municipality of Petrolina, I would like to express my solidarity with its people on this occasion to congratulate them for all they have done for the growth of the Municipality and the Northeast Region.

Despite the growth of the Northeast in recent years, the IBGE, in the 2010 Census, showed that in the North and Northeast, there are 16 million Brazilians living below the poverty line, that is, with a per capita income of R$70.00 per month.

This has led Brazil to have, from today on, the largest integrated plan to combat extreme poverty in its history. At a ceremony held at the Planalto Palace, President Dilma Rousseff launched the "Brazil Without Poverty" plan, which brings together the Federal Government, States, and Municipalities around hundreds of actions aimed at improving the lives of 16 million Brazilians.

Coordinated by the Ministry of Social Development and Hunger Combat, the plan deepens and expands the successful social policy adopted by Brazil in recent years, when 28 million people left poverty and 36 million entered the middle class.

Now, the focus of the work is on the 16 million Brazilians whose family income, divided among its members, does not exceed R$70 per month per person.

Of this total, 59% live in the Northeast, 21% in the South and Southeast, and 20% in the North and Central-West. And no less than 40% are under 14 years of age.

In addition to its solidarity and human aspect, the plan also aims to be a new and powerful lever for Brazil's development. After all, the process of social ascension in the last 8 years was decisive in reducing inequalities, expanding the internal market, strengthening the economy, and accelerating the country's growth. With "Brazil Without Poverty," the government takes on the challenge of ending poverty and, thus, takes a new and decisive step to expand these achievements of all Brazilians.

THE STATE ARRIVING WHERE POVERTY IS

In recent years, the Brazilian government has come closer than ever to the poorest. Thus, 28 million Brazilians left absolute poverty and 36 million entered the middle class.

Even with this effort, 16 million people still remain in extreme poverty. Among other reasons, because there is a poverty so poor that it is hardly reached by the action of the State. It seems to hide, lost in distant grottoes of the

Our vast territory or in segregated zones of large cities.
They are so disadvantaged that they have not even been able to register, let alone participate in well-known social programs like Bolsa Família.
Much less access to essential services such as water, light, education, health, and housing.
The Brazil Without Poverty Plan was created precisely to reach them. To break down social, political, economic, and cultural barriers that segregate people and regions.
Among other things, it will identify and register people who need but do not yet receive Bolsa Família. And help those who already receive it to seek other income sources and improve their living conditions.
To do this, it has developed a new strategy called "Active Search" and is creating the most comprehensive Poverty Map in the country. A map where poverty is not just a number: it has a name, an address, and a surname.
Brazil Without Poverty is also drawing up a National Opportunities Map, identifying the most efficient means for these people to improve their lives.
Only then will our eyes, and the state's arm, reach that so poor poverty that makes it almost invisible.
Thus, the entire country will benefit, as each person who emerges from poverty is a new producer, a new consumer, and above all, a new Brazilian willing to build a new, fairer and more humane Brazil.
Poverty has different faces and needs depending on the region. The reality in the countryside is one thing, in the city another entirely. That is why Brazil Without Poverty will have national and regional actions based on three axes: income, productive inclusion, and public services.
In the countryside, the main objective will be to increase farmers' production. In the city, it will be to qualify labor and identify opportunities and employment for the poorest.
Public programs such as Bolsa Família, Rural Social Security, Brazil Literate, Family Health, Brazil Smiles, More Education, and the Baby Chicken Network, among others, will be expanded and improved throughout the country, as will actions aimed at increasing access for the poorest to public goods and services, including water, light, and housing.
To achieve these goals, the plan is creating the most comprehensive Poverty Map in Brazil. And it is also drawing up an Opportunities Map to identify the most appropriate and efficient means of improving these people's lives.
