I am thinking about the naivety of this country,
which signed the so-called International Framework
Agreement, a convention to reduce cigarette con-
sumption. This agreement even aims to end in the
country the culture of tobacco, a licit drug. If we stop
producing tobacco in this country, with licit con-
sumption of cigarettes, what are we going to do? Im-

I do not smoke. In fact, I want all Brazilians to stop
smoking, for the people of the whole world to stop
smoking, because, as it is an addiction, it damages
health. But I am thinking: how can someone make an

starts with the legalization of marches and, as Depu-

It is inconceivable for this country to advocate for the cultivation of marijuana. There are alternatives, yes. I believe that in the future we may even consider alternatives for tobacco itself. Not today! Today, we defend tobacco cultivation by producers from Rio Grande do Sul, Santa Catarina, and especially Paraná. It is not possible for this automatic substitution to occur. Even the United States and Colombia cultivate alternative crops. This is just a reflection.

It is a topic that we should not even allow to be discussed here: marijuana cultivation in this country, strictly prohibited, when compared to tobacco cultivation in our country.

Mr. President, I want to make this position very clear and realistic regarding who has truly entered the underworld of crime. We know that drug trafficking is today the center of organized crime worldwide, and of course in Brazil.

The discussion is valid, but I am concerned when former President Fernando Henrique Cardoso advocates for the legalization of marijuana, or when the Supreme Federal Court allows the Marijuana March. These are steps we are taking to introduce a drug, in my opinion, destructive to youth and families. We, as Brazilians, cannot allow such barbarity by permitting the cultivation of this drug in our country.

Thank you very much.

The PRESIDENT (Izalci) – I grant the floor, in order, to Deputy Erika Kokay, of the PT of the Federal District.

MS. ERIKA KOKAY (PT-DF. In order. Without revision by the speaker.) – Mr. President, I have closely followed – and I am sure you have as well – what happened in the Federal District regarding the absolute absence of ethics and the promiscuity that has established itself between the public and private spheres.

In various sectors of public policy, we see that there has been a surrender of the state. The state, fragmented, was placed on the table and delivered, slice by slice, to corporate interests. That is why, when I was in the Legislative Assembly, we made every effort to approve a bill that would prevent companies owned by deputies and their family members from bidding or contracting with the state.

Therefore, I am extremely saddened to see that the Constitution and Justice Commission of the Legislative Assembly archived – or did not proceed with – the bill that was being processed in that house, authored by then-deputy Rogério Ulysses.

Mr. President, I believe it is time for us to try to moralize, or actually moralize, the public power. We can no longer allow families

or the companies, when they realize they are facing economic and financial difficulties, decide to run their own children, relatives, or partners as candidates. They run as candidates with the sole objective of resolving their companies' financial problems. This is not a fight for projects, nor a defense of any kind, because democracy allows for the existence of all, but rather a candidate appendage to cost sheets, candidates woven to resolve these companies' financial issues.

This project aimed to establish this moralization, especially because we witnessed scenes we would not have liked to see, in what became known as the "Pandora's Box" operation in the Federal District. We saw emergency contracts being renewed year after year. We saw service-providing company contracts being parceled out and sliced up for various companies. It's as if we were witnessing, Mr. President, the existence of a postmodern hereditary captaincy.

Therefore, it is extremely regrettable the position adopted by the majority in that Committee. The vote of Deputy Chico Leite stands out as an exception, as he voted or positioned in favor of continuing the matter. But the majority of the Constitution and Justice Committee in that House decided to archive this project, deciding to give a seal of approval for this type of procedure, this type of behavior, which damages the morals and ethics of our city.

I would say we need to have Brasília back. This city, thought out, dreamed of, a magical stroke; this city that was supposed to be both functional and ludic, according to Lúcio Costa, needs to be returned to the people who live here.

In this sense, Mr. President, even in the perspective of moralizing public service and moralizing the state's behavior, I presented a project in this House so that we have the same criteria as the "Clean Slate" (Ficha Limpa) regarding the occupation of commissioned posts. We have established criteria that define the minimum for a person's past life, morals, ethics, so that there is a fight in the urn, but this criterion is not given for the occupation of commissioned posts.

Take note, when a candidacy is established, it still goes through the absolutely fundamental and democratic scrutiny of the very population. The scrutiny of the polls is given, but for commissioned posts, there is only the will and decision of the ruler.

That's why I presented a project in this sense, which is currently being processed in this House. We should have strict criteria, which already exist even for those who wish to run for an elected office. That these criteria also apply to the occupation of commissioned posts.
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES

missionaries. I believe that this House, by approving projects of this nature, will have made significant progress towards the goal of no longer having to coexist with a state bent by patrimonial logic, with a state bent by corporate logic. The state, as our Constitution states, must be a portrait of the will of the people themselves, and it exists to serve the people. The goal of the state, in all its spheres, is to ensure that people are seen as people and are imbued with a logic and a living experience of human dignity. We will not achieve this as long as the state is at the mercy of corporate and private interests.

That was it, Mr. President.

BILL NO. 3,795-B, 2004
(Mrs. Laura Carneiro)
Establishes a scholarship, called "stage scholarship", to support undergraduate students, with the counterpart of providing services as interns; with opinions: of the Committee on Labor, Administration, and Public Service, for the approval of this bill and for its incompetence to comment on BILL NO. 4.584/2004, appended (reporter: DEP. VANESSA GRAZZIOTIN); of the Committee on Education and Culture, for the rejection of this bill and BILL NO. 4.584/04, appended (reporter: DEP. ALICE PORTUGAL); and of the Committee on Finance and Taxation, for the non-implication of the matter with an increase or decrease in public revenue or expenditure, not falling within its purview to comment on the financial and budgetary adequacy of this bill, but falling within its purview for BILL NO. 4.584/04, appended; and, on the merits, for the approval of this bill and BILL NO. 4.584/04, appended, with a substitute (reporter: DEP. RICARDO BARROS and substitute reporter: DEP. GUILHERME CAMPOS); and of the Committee on Constitution and Justice and Citizenship, for the illegality of this bill, of BILL NO. 4.584/04, appended, and of the substitute from the Committee on Finance and Taxation (reporter: DEP. LUIZ COUTO).

Disposition: To the Committees on Labor, Administration, and Public Service; Education and Culture; Finance and Taxation (Merit and Art. 54, RICD); and Constitution and Justice and Citizenship (Art. 54, RICD)

Consideration: Proposal subject to plenary consideration – Art. 24, II, "g".

Publication of the Opinions of the Committees on Education and Culture, Finance and Taxation, and Constitution and Justice and Citizenship.

Committee on Education and Culture

I – Report

The main bill, authored by Honorable Deputy Laura Carneiro, aims to establish scholarships for students enrolled in private higher education institutions.

The scholarships would be linked, in whole or in 50%, to the payment of school tuition fees. In the case
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES

From the choice of the 50% formula, the student would receive that portion in cash.

The scholarships established by the proposal, denominated "stage scholarships," would be funded by companies or liberal professionals, to whom students would provide services as interns. The resources employed in this scholarship modality would be deductible from the company's gross income for income tax purposes.

The attached proposal, authored by Honorable Deputy Eduardo Cunha, allows private higher education institutions to deduct from the income tax due, study scholarships granted to students who demonstrate the provision of voluntary service.

II – Relator's Vote

Both bills create new income transfer mechanisms through tax exemptions, from public coffers, directly or indirectly, to private higher education institutions.

In the main bill, the tax exemption aims at the income tax of companies and liberal professionals who, by offering internships to students from private higher education institutions, would remunerate interns with resources linked in whole or in part (50%) to the payment of school tuition fees.

Upon approval of the proposal, winners would be companies, liberal professionals, and private higher education institutions. The first would deduct from income tax the resources for intern compensation. The latter would benefit from an increase in the volume of secure annuities paid and the number of enrolled students.

Students, however, would gain in one way and lose in another. They would gain from an increase in the number of those who would have access to higher education. They would lose, as internships would become linked to school tuition fee payment, which currently does not happen.

Indeed, internships already exist, regulated by Law No. 6,494, of 1997, linked solely to proper academic formation. Companies and liberal professionals currently offer internships to university students to train them in service. Remuneration is entirely in cash, and the student uses it as they see fit.

The necessary association between tax incentives, internships, and school tuition fee payment could stimulate the use of interns as "cheap labor," exactly what Law No. 6,954, of 1997 seeks to avoid.

Public higher education institutions and their students would also emerge as losers, if there is a tax exemption for internships linked to school tuition fee payment.

segments.text:
Annuities, naturally, liberal companies and professionals
would exclude public university students from the stage, and thus, free of charge.
However, the attached bill project No. 4,584, of 2004,
by exempting from income tax the amounts invested in
scholarships, represents another tax incentive beyond those offered by Prouni, with the difference that the reimbursement of the monthly fee would be through the performance of voluntary service. Anyone could receive scholarships, not just those in the cases provided for by Prouni. There would be no need, for example, to prioritize poor students.
The two aforementioned bill projects represent unjustified and costly additions to the existing institutional mechanisms of support for genuinely poor students.
For these reasons, our opinion is unfavorable to both propositions.

The proposal also provides that no labor, social security, or tax obligations shall be imposed on the expenses related to the scholarship mentioned above, and allows the resources allocated to it to be deducted from the company's gross income for income tax purposes.

The bill under review had the law project No. 4,584, 2004, authored by the distinguished Deputy Eduardo Cunha, which provides for the granting of a scholarship to students in private higher education institutions, provided they perform voluntary work, and allows these institutions to deduct the respective amounts from the annual income tax due, within the limits established by specific legislation.

The projects, in accordance with the rules, were distributed to the Commissions on Labor, Administration, and Public Service; Education and Culture; Finance and Taxation; and Constitution, Justice, and Citizenship.

The Commission on Labor, Administration, and Public Service, at its ordinary meeting held on February 22, 2006, unanimously decided to approve Law Project No. 3,795, 2004, and declined its competence to issue an opinion on Law Project No. 4,584, 2004, which was appended.

The Commission on Education and Culture, at its meeting held on November 21, 2007, concluded to reject Law Project No. 3,795, 2004, and its appended project No. 4.584/04.

This is the report.

II – Relator’s Vote
Based on Article 54, in conjunction with Article 32, item X, subitem h, both of the Internal Rules of this House, and the Internal Norm of the Finance and Taxation Commission, which establishes procedures for examining the compatibility or adequacy of budgetary and financial matters, approved on May 29, 1996, this Commission is responsible for examining the proposals, in addition to their merits, regarding their financial and budgetary adequacy.

Upon analyzing Law Project No. 3.795/04, it is observed that, although it proposes to deduct the stage allowance expense from the gross income for income tax purposes and exempts labor, tax, and social security obligations, it does not have budgetary or financial implications, as there is no employment relationship of any kind between the intern and the company that hired them, provided the legal requirements are met.

As per the provisions of articles 3rd and 15th of Law No. 11,788 of September 25, 2008, known as the "Stage Law," if the law recognizes the non-existence of an employment relationship, there are no charges or obligations due. There is merely a professionalizing educational link, supervised by the pedagogical development of the student.

This interpretation is corroborated by Technical Note No. 63/2009 from the Brazilian Federal Revenue Secretariat/Get/Copan, which clarifies that, regarding social security obligations, article 28, paragraph 9, item "i," of Law No. 8.212/91 states that the stipend paid to the intern does not constitute part of the contribution salary and, therefore, "does not form the basis of calculation of the social security contributions due by the employed insured and the company." With regard to tax obligations, the aforementioned technical note considers that the average monthly fees for undergraduate courses do not exceed the exemption limit for IRPF (up to R$ 1,434.59). As for the deductibility of resources used for the stipend from the gross income of companies, the Brazilian Federal Revenue (RFB) understands that such expenses represent "an operational expense of the company, already admitted by accounting and tax rules as deductible from the revenue obtained for the purpose of calculating the profit."

Regarding Project of Law No. 4.584/04, it is evident that the deduction of the value granted under the title of study scholarships from income tax due constitutes a clear renunciation of public revenue of the Union, in conjunction with subnational entities.

In this case, the proposal in question must be accompanied by an estimate of the budgetary and financial impact caused by the renunciation of revenue in the exercise in which the norm should enter into force and in the two subsequent ones, as well as demonstrating its fiscal neutrality by already being considered in the corresponding budgetary law or presenting compensation measures, as required by article 14 of Complementary Law No. 101 of May 4, 2000 (Fiscal Responsibility Law - LRF), as follows:

Article 14. The grant or expansion of tax incentives or benefits from which a revenue renunciation results shall be accompanied by an estimate of the budgetary and financial impact in the exercise in which it should enter into force and in the two following ones, comply with the provisions of the Budgetary Guidelines Law, and meet at least one of the following conditions:

I – demonstration by the proposer that the renunciation was considered in the revenue estimate of the budgetary law, in accordance with article 12, and that it will not affect the fiscal results goals provided in the annex of the Budgetary Guidelines Law;
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES

II – be accompanied by compensation measures, during the period mentioned in the heading, through the increase in revenue, from the elevation of rates, expansion of the calculation base, augmentation or creation of a tax or contribution.

§ 1. Renunciation includes amnesty, remission, subsidy, presumed credit, grant of non-general exemption, rate alteration or modification of the calculation base that involves discriminatory reduction of taxes or contributions, and other benefits corresponding to differentiated treatment.

§ 2. If the act of granting or expanding the incentive or benefit referred to in the heading of this article results from the condition contained in subparagraph II, the benefit will only come into effect when the measures referred to in that subparagraph are implemented. (we have emphasized)

Law No. 11,768 of August 14, 2008 (Budget Guidelines Law for 2009 - LDO 2009), in its Article 93, also ratifies the requirements of the above-quoted provision:

Article 93. A bill or provisional measure that grants or expands a tax incentive or benefit shall only be approved or issued if the requirements of Article 14 of Complementary Law No. 101 of 2000 are met.

Therefore, the aforementioned Technical Note No. 63/2009 from RFB estimates the "potential revenue renunciation" of IRPJ at R$ 54 million, R$ 59 million, R$ 65 million, and R$ 71 million, for each exercise of the period from 2009 to 2012, respectively.

However, Project of Law No. 4.584/04 does not present compensation measures, or at least indicates that the renunciation was considered in the revenue estimate of the budget law, as required by subparagraphs I and II of Article 14 of the LRF.

The project does not offer compensatory measures that make it fiscally neutral, which is why it cannot be considered suitable and compatible in budgetary and financial terms.

The fact is that the budget law for the 2009 financial year - LOA/2009, Law No. 11,897 of December 30, 2008, contains an innovative compensation mechanism for budgetary-financial impacts resulting from the issuance of permanent legislation that gives rise to revenue renunciations from tax benefits or exemptions, as in this case.

LOA/2009 has in its work program, a budgetary unit for Contingency Reserve, specific credit for the compensation of revenue offloads, also called revenue or tax expenditure renunciations, as follows:

90.000 – Contingency Reserve –
0999.0E61.0001 – Reserve for Compensation of

Bill Projects that Establish Tax Exemptions
Subject to Deliberation by a Collective Body of the
Legislative Power during the Budgetary-Financial
Compatibility Examination - NA.
The credit mentioned has a provision of R$ 94 million, GND 9 (contingency), with a financing source of 100 (Ordinary Resources of the Treasury), application modality 90 (Direct), and primary result identifier 1 (mandatory expenditure).
It is noteworthy that the provision is qualified by the budgetary law as a mandatory expenditure, in accordance with the description provided by the Executive Power in its Complementary Information to PLOA/2009, Annex III, item I, as per Law No. 11.768/2008 - LDO/2009.
Although it is recognized that the amount allocated for compensation is insufficient to meet the needs and demands presented by society to the state, as can be identified from the values conveyed in the proposals that are being processed by the Houses of the National Congress, the reserve established there represents a beginning, a milestone in the incipient connection between the ordinary and budgetary legislative processes.
In this regard, we propose the appropriation of R$ 54 million from the provision in the budgetary credit 90.000.0999.0E61.0001, as established in Law No. 11.897 of December 30, 2008, the Budgetary Law for the 2009 fiscal year, to demonstrate that its renunciation was considered in the current budgetary estimate, ensuring its fiscal neutrality for the purposes of Article 14, I, of Complementary Law No. 101 of 2000.
In the same vein, in order to ensure the future compensation for the renunciation and other ones that this legislative body deems worthy of compensation, we present amendments (Amendments No. 0008 and 0009) to the Mixed Committee on Plans, Public Budgets, and Oversight - CMO regarding the Preliminary Report of PLN 46/2009, the Budgetary Proposal for the 2010 financial year, so that the reserve of resources for benefits or incentives of a non-tax nature, but also financial, credit, or patrimonial, with the respective provision, to be defined by the CMO, is included in that Law.
We inform that the amendments were fully accepted by the CMO and are now included in item 18.1.11 of Part B of the Preliminary Opinion, with the following wording:
18. It is prohibited to present amendments by the rapporteur aimed at including new subtitles or increasing the value of provisions in the 2010 Budgetary Proposal, except for the reasons stated in this Preliminary Opinion.
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES

18.1. Based on Article 144, paragraph III, of Resolution 01/2006-CN, the provisions of item 18 do not apply to the initiatives of the General Rapporteur to enable:
18.1.11. the creation of a Reserve to address legislative proposals granting tax, financial, credit, or property benefits that result in revenue renouncements during the 2010 fiscal year, subject to the deliberations of a permanent legislative body during the budgetary and financial adequacy review; (emphasized)

Additionally, item 26 of Part B of the Preliminary Opinion of PLOA/2010 ensures the necessary resources for implementing the approved measure, as follows:
26. From the total available funds, R$ 20,695,140,000 (twenty billion, six hundred ninety-five million and fourteen thousand reais) will be deducted for the following purposes:
26.2. Expenses outlined in items 18.1.2 to 18.1.12 of this Opinion and other General Rapporteur amendments (item 17.1 of this Opinion): R$ 13,270,140,000 (thirteen billion, two hundred seventy million and fourteen thousand reais). (emphasized)

Regarding the merits, we recognize the relevance and opportunity of the matter, as it combines academic study with practical experience through voluntary service to companies and the community. The existence of similar mechanisms, such as PROUNI, identified by CEC as a reason for rejecting the proposals, does not preclude the desirability of adopting the instrument under review. The proposals aim to associate study with work. However, Article 93 of LDO/2009 requires a maximum validity period of 5 years. In this regard, we present an Alternative Text setting this limit, effective from its publication, and reconciling the two proposals under consideration.

Thus, I invite my colleagues to inaugurate the parliamentary prerogative of generating medium and long-term public policies by approving this simple but emblematic proposal, with the amendment for consideration by this Committee.

For the reasons stated, I submit my vote against the budgetary and financial implications of House Bill No. 3,795, 2004, and in favor of the financial and budgetary adequacy of its appended House Bill No. 4,584, 2004, and, on the merits, in favor of approving both, in accordance with the Alternative Text presented to this Committee.

Committee Room, 2009. – Deputy Ricardo Barros, Rapporteur.

Preliminarily, it is noted that the Project of Law No. 5,717, 2005, violates Article 61, § 1, item II, subitem “e” of the Federal Constitution. This provision stipulates that the initiative for a law aiming to create public administration bodies is a exclusive attribute of the President of the Republic.

At this point, Article 8 of the Internal Norms of the Commission of Finance and Taxation, which establishes procedures for examining budget and financial compatibility or adequacy, states that "a proposal that increases expenses in matters of exclusive initiative of the President of the Republic will be considered incompatible" (emphasis added).

It is also verified that the proposal under review, in the light of Article 17 of the Fiscal Responsibility Law - LRF (Complementary Law No. 101/2000), imposes a legal obligation on the entity for a period exceeding two fiscal years, constituting a continuous mandatory expense. Thus, according to § 1 of the aforementioned provision, "acts that create or increase the expense referred to in the caput shall be accompanied by the estimate provided for in Article 16, item I, and demonstrate the source of resources for its financing." Article 16, item I, stipulates:

Art. 16. The creation, expansion or improvement of government action that entails an increase in expenses shall be accompanied by:
I - an estimate of the budgetary and financial impact in the exercise in which it is to enter into force and in the two subsequent ones.

In the same sense, Law No. 12,309, of August 9, 2010 (LDO 2011), provides:

Art. 91. Legislative proposals, in the form of bills, legislative decrees or provisional measures that imply or authorize a decrease in Union revenue or an increase in expenses for the 2011 exercise, shall be accompanied by estimates of these effects, for each of the exercises included in the period from 2011 to 2013, detailing the respective calculation memorandum and corresponding compensation, in accordance with the constitutional and legal provisions that govern the matter.

In corroboration with the understanding of the aforementioned provisions, the Commission of Finance and Taxation issued Summary No. 1, 2008, which considers incompatible and inadequate a proposal, even if of an authorizing nature, that fails to estimate the budgetary and financial impact and demonstrate the source of resources for its financing, as follows:

Regarding the examination of the proposal's adequacy with the Multi-annual Plan – PPA 2008-2011, it is found that there is no specific action for the implementation of the Federal University of Serra Geral in Bahia within Program 1073 – Brazil University. **DISPOSITION**

The Federal Congress establishes the Constitutional Fund for Northern Financing – FNO, the Constitutional Fund for Northeast Financing – FNE, and the Constitutional Fund for Central-West Financing – FCO, and provides other measures; having received opinions: from the Commission on Economic Development, Industry, and Commerce, for approval (report by DEP. LAUREZ MOREIRA); and from the Commission on Amazon, National Integration, and Regional Development, for approval with a substitute (report by DEP. VALTENIR PEREIRA).

**ORDER**

To the Commissions on Economic Development, Industry, and Commerce; Amazon, National Integration, and Regional Development; Finance and Taxation (Merit and Art. 54, RICD); and Constitution and Justice and Citizenship (Art. 54 RICD).

**CONSIDERATION**

The proposal is subject to conclusive consideration by the Commissions – Art. 24, II.

**PUBLICATION OF THE COMMISSION'S OPINION ON AMAZON, NATIONAL INTEGRATION, AND REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT**

I – Report

Bill No. 1,097, of 2007, originating from the Federal Senate, amends Article 4 of Law No. 7,827, of September 27, 1989, which regulates Article 159, paragraph I, subparagraph "c", of the Federal Constitution, which established the Constitutional Fund for Northern Financing – FNO, the Constitutional Fund for Northeast Financing – FNE, and the Constitutional Fund for Central-West Financing – FCO, and provides other measures.

The new text proposed for the heading of this provision now includes the commercial and service sectors of the Northern, Northeast, and Central-West Regions in the list of productive activities eligible for resources from the respective Constitutional Financing Funds.

The proposal also repeals Article 4, paragraph 3, of Law No. 7,827, of 1989, and adds a new paragraph to the same Article 4 of that Law, stipulating that the financing limits for the productive activities referred to in the heading of this Article shall be defined in the annual financing program referred to in Article 14, paragraph II, of the same Law.

The proposal was analyzed and approved by the Commission on Economic Development, Industry, and Commerce.

No amendments were presented to this Commission within the regulatory time frame.

This is the report.

II – Relator's Vote
The proposed legislation amends Article 4 of Law No. 7,827, 1989, to include trade and service provision among the economic activities eligible for resources from the Constitutional Funds.

The law in question regulates Article 159, paragraph I, item "c", of the Federal Constitution, which established the Constitutional Funds for Financing the North, Northeast, and Central-West, respectively, FNO, FNE, and FCO.

The aforementioned constitutional provision allocates 3% of the revenue from income and provents taxes on industrialized products for application in financing programs for productive sectors in the North, Northeast, and Central-West regions.

Consequently, these funds annually allocate financial resources to these regions for long-term investments or even as working capital or operating costs, with lower financial charges than market rates, all with the aim of complementing and enhancing regional productive capacity through strategic projects.

The objective is to promote economic and social development in areas with low Human Development Index (HDI) and also to stimulate regional economic potential, seeking greater efficiency in resource allocation to increase enterprise productivity, generate new jobs, enhance tax revenue, and improve income distribution.

With the proposed amendments to the text submitted by the Federal Senate, now under review, trade and service activities are brought on par with the agricultural, mining, industrial, and agro-industrial sectors, as productive activities listed in the opening of Article 4 of Law No. 7,827, 1989. This is because the proposal also aims to delete paragraph 3 of the same article 4, which stipulates that Constitutional funds allocated to these funds may only finance commercial and service enterprises up to 20% of the resources planned for each year.

The extension of credit instruments to other economic sectors in all regions benefiting from Constitutional Funds, as contained in the legislation submitted by the Federal Senate, should be analyzed, as far as possible, from the perspective of the legislator when establishing the Constitutional Funds.

The goal was then to foster the country's development policy to correct regional imbalances.
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES

Regional books, in compliance with the constitutional objective set forth in Article 3, Section II of the Federal Constitution. Thus, it sought to ensure sufficient resources for the less dynamic regions of the country to induce investments in productive sectors, with a view to social growth and development.

The resources obtained through these funds are primarily intended for financing priority sectors within the framework of the National Regional Development Policy, such as the industrial, agro-industrial, tourism, technology and innovation, family agriculture, among others. Over the years, the injection of resources has generated positive effects for the benefited regions, contributing to increased employment, diversification of the productive base, restructuring and densification of productive chains, and greater participation of micro and small enterprises in the economy.

Therefore, the beneficial effects of the Constitutional Funds are visible and necessary today in light of the significant impacts of the planned and ongoing structural investments in these regions, particularly from the substantial public investments in infrastructure within the Acceleration of Growth Program, as well as due to the increased purchasing power of the population, a consequence of successful social programs.

These factors contribute to the formation and structuring of new productive chains and arrangements in these regions, such as the new hydroelectric power plants on the Madeira River, refineries, automobile assembly plants, shipyards, steel plants, among other structural investments.

With the aim of intensifying and internalizing the effects of the new, vibrant productive chains that are forming and require, it is necessary to maintain the previously established limitations for the trade and services sector, that is, at the maximum level of 20%, as provided for in Article 4, Section 3 of Law No. 7,827 of 1989.

It is worth noting, by the way, that the inclusion of these sectors in the opening of Article 4 of the aforementioned law would lead to competition between them and the priority sectors for regional development; precisely those that demand significant structural investments and greater attention from the State. This is not only due to the essence of the Constitutional Funds, but also to the positive perspectives for the productive sectors of the North, Northeast, and Central-West regions.

Add to this a growing process of deindustrialization observed throughout the country, which is due, among other factors, to the currency appreciation and the high production costs. This process contributes

for the loss of competitiveness of consumer goods-producing industries, especially due to the growing influx of products from the Asian continent, benefiting only the commercial sector.
The greater concentration of resources from Constitutional Financing Funds in the productive sector and in the primary goods transformation industry will not only enable the maintenance of competitiveness but also attract new businesses to the regions covered, decentralizing spatially the country's productive map.
It is important to clarify that we are not positioning ourselves against the injection of resources into trade and service sectors. On the contrary, the importance of these activities for the country's development is evident. But we must be consistent with the legislator's intent when dealing with the destinies of Constitutional Funds.
Therefore, we understand that equating the trade and service provision sectors with other activities benefiting from Constitutional Funds, such as structural investments (industry, refineries, etc.) - as proposed by the bill under review - would imply a disincentive to national economic growth.
This is because, given the current economic scenario and what is expected until the end of the decade, there would inevitably be a reduction in resources directed towards primary goods transformation activities, which were previously a priority, since there would be no financing limit for commercial and service ventures, blurring the distinction between heavy and structural investments.
Furthermore, we would be deviating from the true purpose of Constitutional Funds, as banks would prioritize investments related to trade and service sectors due to the quick return on loans made, or the immediate turnover of credit transactions.
On the other hand, and despite the arguments presented above, it is impossible not to recognize the quite specific reality of the Federal District, when compared to other federal units covered by Article 4 of Law 7,827, of 1989. The service sector and commercial activities are the Federal District's economic vocation par excellence.
Therefore, considering the specificities of this federal unit - so well described in the Senate's considerations - we understand it necessary to add a new paragraph to Article 4 of the cited law, to deal exclusively with the Federal District.
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES

In this new paragraph, the limit for the financing of commercial and service ventures may reach the maximum level of 40% of the annual resources allocated to the Constitutional Fund for Central-West Financing, at the discretion of the development agency of the Region.

PROJECT OF LAW No. 1.962-A, of 2007
(From Mr. Antonio Bulhões)
Amends Law No. 9.985, of July 18, 2000, which establishes the National System of Nature Conservation Units; with the opinion of the Mining and Energy Committee, for approval with a substitute (Rapporteur: DEP. BERNARDO SANTANA DE VASCONCELLOS).

Order: To the Mining and Energy, Environment and Sustainable Development, and Constitution and Citizenship Committees (Article 54 RICD).

Consideration: Proposal Subject to Conclusive Consideration by the Committees - Article 24 II

Publication of the Mining and Energy Committee's Opinion

I - Report

Project of Law No. 1.962, of 2007, authored by the noble Deputy Antonio Bulhões, proposes amendments to Law No. 9.985, of July 18, 2000, which establishes the National System of Nature Conservation Units, through the addition of § 7 to Article 17 and new redaction to §§ 3 and 4 of Article 22, all of the aforementioned law.

Article 17 of Law No. 9.985, of 2000, deals with national forests, considered conservation units for sustainable use. In this context, the article's caption defines a national forest as "an area with native forest cover of predominantly native species and whose basic objective is sustainable multiple use."
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES

"Of the forest resources and scientific research, with emphasis on methods for the sustainable exploration of native forests." The unit of this category, when created by the state or municipality, as stipulated in the article, shall be designated, respectively, State Forest and Municipal Forest.

National Forest, as regulated in the aforementioned article, is public property and will have a Consultative Council, chaired by the body responsible for its administration and by representatives of public bodies, civil society organizations, and, where applicable, traditional residents.

The Law Project No. 1,962, of 2007, by inserting a § 7th to Article 17 of Law No. 9,985, of 2000, aims to regulate, within the scope of said law, the exploration of the subsoil in National, State, or Municipal Forests, as follows:

- Compliance with environmental licensing norms;
- Ensuring the consultation of the respective Consultative Council;
- The management plan must provide for the exploration of the subsoil;
- Conditions the exploration to the acquisition of an adjacent area to the unit, with an extent not inferior to that to be explored, if the vegetation is in a better or equivalent conservation state to that intended for mining, or with an extent equal to twice the explored one, if the vegetation's conservation state is inferior, and the lands must be donated to the public entity responsible for the National, State, or Municipal Forest for incorporation into it.

Article 22 of Law No. 9,985, of 2000, deals with the creation, by public act, of conservation units.

§ 3rd of Article 22 addresses the public consultation process, preceding the creation of the conservation unit, as provided for in § 2nd of the same article. The current text determines that in the consultation process, the public entity is required to provide adequate and understandable information to the local population and other interested parties.

§ 4th of Article 22 dispenses from the consultation process the creation of an Ecological Station or Biological Reserve.

Law Project No. 1,962, of 2007, by conferring new wording to §§ 3rd and 4th of said Article 22, seeks:

- Regarding § 3rd of Article 22, to add to the current wording, the need for the public entity to make the information available through the worldwide computer network, presenting it at a public hearing in the region where the conservation unit is intended to be created.

In his Justification, the author of the bill informs the need for greater detail in two aspects of Law No. 9,985, of 2000, given the existence of interpretations that deviate from the objectives and guidelines of the Law of the National System of Conservation Units (SNUC).
The first aspect concerns mining in national forests. He informs that currently there are 7 national forests with licensed mining activity and another 11 with potential for mineral exploration. Although he acknowledges that there is no explicit prohibition of mining in this category of sustainable use unit in Law No. 9,985, of 2000, and that mineral resources are Union property under Article 20, X, of the Federal Constitution, he emphasizes the environmental impact of mining activity, which is subject to differentiated treatment under Article 225, Section 2, of the Magna Carta.
Regarding the second aspect, he addresses two cases: the first deals with the impossibility of access by low-income populations or more remote locations (where many protected areas are created) to computer resources, making it necessary to hear the local population; the second concerns the unavailability of technical information that prompted the environmental agency to create the unit, making it necessary to make such information available on the worldwide web.
Finally, considering that the Private Natural Heritage Reserve is created on private lands, by the meritorious intention of its owner, and that there is no act of expropriation or land use restriction by neighboring properties, it is perfectly dispensable to conduct a public consultation.
This is the report.

II – Relator's Vote
Upon evaluating the merits of Bill No. 1,962, of 2007.

Despite the usual brilliance of the author of the proposal and his admirable effort to contribute to sustainability, an objective of us all, some important points regarding the matters addressed in his proposal must be analyzed in the light of the legislation in force that deals with the central points of Bill 1.962/2007.

It is important to transcribe Article 225 CF/88, in the parts relevant to the reported process and duly highlighted to draw attention to the points that underpin the reflection that now arises:

"Article 225. Everyone has the right to an ecologically balanced environment, a public good. The form and the conditions of its use shall be defined by law, taking into account the preservation of natural resources necessary for the well-being of present and future generations."
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES

Common to the people and essential to a healthy quality of life, it imposes on public power and the community the duty to defend and preserve it for present and future generations.

§ 1. To ensure the effectiveness of this right, it is the responsibility of public power:

(...)

III – to define, in all units of the Federation, territorial spaces and their components to be specially protected, with alterations and suppressions only permitted through law, and any use that compromises the integrity of the attributes justifying their protection is prohibited;

IV – to require, in accordance with the law, for the installation of a work or activity potentially causing significant environmental degradation, a prior environmental impact study, the contents of which shall be made public;

§ 2. Those who exploit mineral resources are obligated to rehabilitate degraded environments, in accordance with the technical solution required by the competent public authority, as provided by law.

(...)

§ 5. Lands returned or seized by the states due to discriminatory actions, necessary for the protection of natural ecosystems, are indisponible.

The 1988 Federal Constitution, in Article 225, §1, III, established that the public power should define "in all units of the Federation, territorial spaces and their components to be specially protected, with alterations and suppressions only permitted through law...".

With this objective, Law No. 9.985, of July 18, 2000, which establishes the National System of Nature Conservation Units - SNUC, was created.

Article 17 of Law No. 9.985/2000 (SNUC) deals with national forests, considered conservation units for sustainable use. The article defines them as "an area with native forest cover and has as its main objective the sustainable multiple use of forest resources and scientific research, with an emphasis on sustainable methods of exploring native forests." It also stipulates that their domain will be of the Union, or of the states, or of the municipalities, depending on which of these entities is responsible for their creation.

In addition to defining the public domain of these areas, it provides for the existence of an advisory council and defines its composition, seeking the equal participation of all segments of society.

As already stated in the report, the proposal in question aims to:

- Comply with the regulations governing environmental licensing;
- Ensure the consultation of the respective advisory council;
- The management plan should address the exploitation of the subsoil;
- Condition the acquisition of contiguous land to the unit, with an area not less than that to be exploited, if the vegetation is in a better or equivalent conservation state to that intended for mining, or with an area twice as large as that exploited, if the vegetation's conservation state is inferior, with the land to be donated to the public entity responsible for the national, state, or municipal forest, for incorporation into it.

The author of the proposal himself reports that there is no explicit prohibition in the Law of the SNUC (National System of Conservation Units) regarding mining in these areas, on the contrary, he informs of existing and ongoing mining projects in these areas. This could not be otherwise.

The author's argument that the exploitation of mineral resources conflicts with the principle of sustainability, as exploiting such resources leads to their depletion, arguing for the impossibility of sustainable use of these resources, and that mining has a high environmental impact, worthy of mention in the Federal Constitution, specifically in the chapter on the environment, referring in this case to Article 225, paragraph 2, "Those who exploit mineral resources are obligated to rehabilitate the degraded environment, in accordance with the technical solution required by the competent public authority, as provided by law."

In the humble opinion of this rapporteur, with all due respect, these affirmations do not hold, for the reasons to be exposed.

First, one must define the difference between sustainability and untouchability.

Sustainability aims to regulate human activities in a harmonious manner, observing three fundamental principles: social welfare, economic factor, and preservation of natural resources. Man is part of the environment and promotes, with respect to these pillars, its transformation.

Untouchability considers natural resources of all kinds as sacred, with an impossible and impassible use of any kind of exploitation. Man is considered per se as a threat to this set of goods.

Sustainability, from the perspective of productive enterprises, is presented in the triangle whose vertices are economic viability, social responsibility, and environmental responsibility.
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES

This rapporteur understands the term sustainable development to be a pleonasm, a redundancy, as if it is not sustainable, it is not development, it is stagnation. In this context, Mining, unlike justified in the presentation of the project under review, is more than possible, necessary and indispensable from the perspective of sustainability, but impossible from the perspective of untouchability.

The most renowned doctrinarians defend that there are no conflicts between constitutional norms and that when it seems that a provision conflicts with another, we only have an apparent conflict between these norms, since there is a harmonious interconnection between them that forms the set of the greater norm and the guidelines that guide the social pact of coexistence of our nation, in all its nuances.

Therefore, these apparent conflicts between norms should be resolved through the interpretation of what our Constitution brings in its entirety, using its principles and dispositions as vectors in the final solution of the supposed impasse. We must also do this in the observation of the present project under review.

We therefore observe these points that guide us in this important mission when analyzing the present law project.

“Article 20. The property of the Union includes:
(...)
II - abandoned lands indispensable to the defense of borders, fortifications and military constructions, federal communication routes and environmental preservation, defined by law;
(...)
IX - mineral resources, including those of the subsoil;”

Therefore, it is important to note that we are dealing in this project with assets that belong to the Union, both in the case of national forests and in the case of mineral resources.

Using vital precepts for the analysis we are making, in compliance with the constitutional text, it is important to observe Title VII - Of Economic and Financial Order, Chapter I - General Principles of Economic Activity:

“Article 170. The economic order, founded on the valorization of human labor and free initiative, aims to ensure to all a dignified existence, in accordance with the precepts of social justice, observing the following principles:
(...)
VI - protection of the environment, including through differentiated treatment according to the environmental impact of products and services and their production and provision processes;

VII – reduction of regional and social inequalities;
VIII – pursuit of full employment; (...)

Unique Paragraph. Everyone is guaranteed the free exercise of any economic activity, regardless of public agency authorization, except in cases provided by law.

(...)

Article 176. Mines, whether in operation or not, and other mineral resources, as well as hydraulic energy potential, constitute a separate property from that of the soil, for the purposes of exploration or utilization, and belong to the Union, the concessionary being guaranteed the property of the product of the mine.

§ 1. The exploration and extraction of mineral resources and the utilization of the potentials referred to in the preceding paragraph may only be carried out with authorization or concession from the Union, in the national interest, by Brazilians or a company constituted under Brazilian laws and having its headquarters and administration in the country, in accordance with the law that will establish specific conditions when these activities are developed in a border area or indigenous lands.

§ 2. The soil owner shall be entitled to a share of the results of the mine, in the form and value determined by law.

§ 3. Exploration authorization shall always be for a determined period, and the authorizations and concessions provided for in this article may not be ceded or transferred, in whole or in part, without the prior consent of the granting authority.

Article 177. The Union's monopoly includes:

I – exploration and extraction of oil and natural gas deposits and other fluid hydrocarbons; (...)

V – exploration, extraction, enrichment, reprocessing, industrialization, and trade of mineral resources and nuclear minerals and their derivatives, except for isotopes whose production, marketing, and use may be authorized under a permit regime, as provided for in article 21, paragraph XXIII, items b and c, of this Federal Constitution.

Mining in Brazil – economic and environmental aspects:

The search, exploration, and utilization of mineral resources have been part of human history, including the discovery of Brazil, when
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES

In Europe, mercantilist practices of metal trade prevailed.

Brazil's history, including its territorial occupation, has a close relationship with the search, exploration, and utilization of mineral resources.

There is no doubt that Brazil has extremely favorable geological environments for the discovery of mineral deposits, which have always placed us, since the discovery, in a prominent position in the ranking of world mineral reserves.

Initially, in our history, we were hit by a reckless extractive exploitation of our mineral resources by the Portuguese Empire; later, mining became a basic sector for the country's development, with reflections on GDP, job creation, and trade balance. Beyond the economic context, the mining activity has been operating with social and environmental responsibility, in a sustainability context.

The impossibility of envisioning, in the current stage of humanity, a modern life without the use of products and derivatives of mineral resources is highlighted. This fact was even recognized by the signatories of the "Rio + 10" Conference, which also considered mining a fundamental activity for the socio-economic development of many countries, including Brazil.

In this context, the primary constituent elevated mineral resources, including those of the subsoil, to the category of Union property.

In the same vein, it considered deposits, whether in operation or not, and other mineral resources as a distinct property from that of the soil, belonging to the Union, for the purpose of exploration or utilization. Furthermore, it determined that research and mining are objects of authorization or concession by the Union, in the national interest. And, aware of the relevance of mining for the country's development, as well as the environmental impacts caused by it, it sought to ensure that the exploration and utilization of mineral resources did not constitute a permanent environmental liability, obliging the explorer of such resources to recover the degraded environment, in accordance with Article 225, § 2 of the Magna Carta.

In addition, currently, mining activity is carried out with social and environmental responsibility. Regarding the latter, it is necessary to clarify that mining, in general, is subject to a set of guidelines and regulations at the three levels of power, and is one of the activities with the highest level of inspection and control by the competent bodies.

Public audiences and non-governmental entities for environmental protection.

In conclusion:

Therefore, regarding Article 1 of Project Law 1.962/2007, we conclude the following:

As both national forests and mineral resources in the Brazilian subsurface are federal property, and given that mining is a monopoly of the Union, the licensing process must consider the environmental impact of mining activities, ensuring the balance between economic development and environmental preservation.
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES

The union of the definition of destination and use of these assets, and already being defined in infra-constitutional legislation, the entire system of definition, use, and form would be unreasonable to require a provision in a management plan for mineral resources in national forests. Since the Union grants or denies the exploration of these resources, which are its monopoly, and both (national forests and subsoil/mineral resources) are assets under its domain. An asset is something that has value, and mineral resources are Union assets, even constituting a distinct property of the soil. The unavailability of their use removes their value, causing them to cease to be assets, and infringing on the interests of the collective.

All legislation dealing with mining activity already defines the permitted forms of exploration, and the licensing processes already include environmental impact studies and reports that may occur. An example of this is the requirement for an EIA/RIMA (Environmental Impact Assessment/Environmental Impact and Environmental Management Report). The aforementioned licensing processes also define all measures to mitigate environmental impact and establish a recovery plan for affected areas, in order to restore these areas to their previous status quo before exploration.

Just for information, I cite infra-constitutional legislation at the federal level that deals with mining activity and the environment (remembering that mining is subject to a set of regulations, where the three levels of state power have attributes regarding mining and the environment):

- Mining Code (Decree-Law No. 227, of 28/02/1967 and its amendments)
- Law No. 6,938, of 31-8-81 and its amendments, which establishes the National Policy on the Environment
- Law No. 9,537, of 11-12-97 and its amendments, which regulates works, dredging, and mineral research and mining along the borders of Brazilian jurisdictional waters
- Decree No. 97,632, of 10-4-89, which provides for the recovery plan for areas degraded by mining
- Decree No. 99,724, of 6-6-90, which regulates Law 6.938/81
- CONAMA Resolution No. 01, of 23-1-86, which establishes basic criteria and general guidelines for EIA/RIMA
- CONAMA Resolution No. 09, of 6-12-90, which provides specific norms for obtaining an environmental license for the extraction of minerals, except those for immediate use in civil construction
- CONAMA Resolution No. 010, of 6-12-90, which provides for the establishment of specific criteria

Brazilian, and that this advertising should be given in the best way to reach its target audience.

I share the understanding of the distinguished author that the creation of a Private Natural Heritage Reserve (PNHR) arises from the noble intention of the private land owner.

It is important to note that the mere intention of the owner does not suffice to create a PNHR; it is necessary for there to be, on site, a diversity of biology (defined in Article 2, clause III of the Law of the National System of Conservation Units - SNUC) that justifies the creation of the conservation unit. And, as a conservation unit, the PNHR is not only permanently registered but is also strictly subject to a series of procedural and regulatory implications, including normative ones, aimed at preserving and conserving the ecosystems, species, and natural habitats present in the PNHR.

The constitutional principles guide the "mens legis," constituting a limitation on the legislator's actions. In this context, the principle of equality, enshrined in our Magna Carta, stands out; it is not enough for the legislator to ensure that the law is clear and objective; he must also ensure that its application by the interpreter is done with equality.

Therefore, it is the legislator's responsibility not only to provide equal normative treatment to situations of equality but also to provide unequal normative treatment to situations of inequality; primarily, he must ensure that this treatment is justified, reasonable, proportional, feasible, and effective.

Under this perspective, as a parliamentarian and as a citizen, I am fully aware of how the exercise of the legislative power reflects and impacts, directly and indirectly, the life of Brazilian society, of which we are legitimate representatives.

Thus, imbued with a spirit of collaboration and guided by the principles that govern parliamentary action, as enshrined in the Magna Carta, I consider it necessary to adjust the Law of SNUC, regarding conservation units, in order to harmonize and standardize equivalent situations, currently treated normatively in a context of inequality that is not justifiable.

I believe that the total or partial transformation of the conservation unit into units of the Integral Protection Group or the Sustainable Use Group, provided that the procedures outlined in Article 22, clause 2 of the SNUC Law are followed, should be carried out through a normative instrument of the same hierarchical level that created it.

In the same vein, the geographical boundary alteration of the unit (reduction), in accordance with the terms of this proposal, should be carried out through a normative instrument of the same hierarchical level.

In accordance with the SNUC law for expanding the UC,
this expansion should also be carried out through a normative instrument of the same hierarchical level that created it.
Based on my understanding, it is necessary to confer dynamism to situations inherent to the creation and adaptation of conservation units,
in order to ensure the effectiveness of the right to a balanced ecological environment, as stipulated in Article 225 of the Constitution.
Considering that it is constitutionally the responsibility of the public power to ensure the effectiveness of this right,
by defining territorial spaces and their components to be specially protected, it is coherent to allow the entity responsible for creating a conservation unit
to, in a simplified manner and using a normative instrument of the same hierarchical level as the creation, transform it totally or partially
into an Integral Protection Group unit or a Sustainable Use Group unit, as the case may be.
This understanding also applies to adjustments, if necessary, regarding geographical limits (expansion or reduction).
Furthermore, the normative instrument for creating a unit comprises only a formal instrument,
which cannot override the administrative procedure preceding the creation, the latter being notably critical and relevant.
Thus, there is no doubt that the creation or transformation of a unit by the responsible entity is preceded by a critical and well-founded procedure,
in an "obligation-power" act in favor of a balanced environment. In this context, the formalization of the act does not hinder the action of the public power.
Now, if the public power can create a unit by decree, there is no reason to condition that its territorial adjustment or transformation
be carried out through a different normative instrument.
Finally, based on legal security and in compliance with the constitutional norm,
I understand that the disaffection of a conservation unit directly affects the established relations under its creation, in all aspects (environmental, social, and economic),
and should be limited to exceptional cases, and still be the object of extensive debate by the entire society. In this sense, it is justified that the disaffection be carried out through a specific law.
In light of the considerations presented, I vote in favor of the approval of PL No. 1,962, of 2007, as amended.
Commission Room, April 20, 2011. - Deputy Bernardo Santana de Vasconcellos, Rapporteur.

EDUCATION AND CULTURE COMMISSION

Winning Report

I - Report

The examined bill aims to authorize the Executive Branch to create the Federal University of the City of Goiás-GO, through the dismemberment of the Federal University of Goiás (UFG).

The matter was processed in the Commission on Labor, Administration and Public Service (CTASP), where it received a favorable report from Deputy Carlos Alberto Leréia.

Within the Commission on Education and Culture (CEC), Deputy Geraldo Resende offered a favorable report on the proposal, which was rejected at the ordinary meeting on October 28, 2009.

It now falls to us, designated by the CEC Presidency, to draft the winning report and the recommendation to be sent to the Executive Branch.

II - Relator's Vote

This Commission has consistently followed a set procedure when considering matters of this nature, based on its 2001 Recommendation to Relators (revised in 2007), which states:

"Since it involves the creation of public bodies, and therefore positions, functions, and jobs, and because it entails increased expenditure, the legislative initiative to create schools, at any level or in any mode of instruction, is exclusive to the Executive Branch (see Art. 61, § 1, II, of the Federal Constitution).

Bills of this nature are merely authorizing and, therefore, inoperative, as they do not generate rights or obligations.

(...)

Thus, the report of a Relator on a PL aiming to create a public school, at any level or in any mode of instruction, should conclude with a rejection of the proposal.

The creation of schools should be suggested in a proposal of the type INDICATION, to be forwarded to the Executive Branch."

"Nothing to the Executive Power. (See art. 113 of the Internal Regulation of the Chamber of Deputies). Even considering that this proposal has a peculiar character by authorizing the Executive Power to create the Federal University of the City of Goiás-GO, through the dismemberment of an already existing university, in this case, the Federal University of Goiás (UFG), our position, supported by the Commission, is for the rejection of the matter.

At this juncture, we have drafted an Indication to the Executive Power suggesting the creation of the Federal University of the City of Goiás, within the context of the educational policy of expanding higher education, implemented by the current Federal Government.

Committee Room, October 28, 2009. - Deputy Pedro Wilson, Rapporteur.

REQUEST
(From the Committee on Education and Culture)
Requests the forwarding of an Indication to the Executive Power, regarding the creation of the Federal University of the City of Goiás-GO, through the dismemberment of the Federal University of Goiás.

Mr. President:
In accordance with art. 113, item I and § 1 of the Internal Regulation of the Chamber of Deputies, I request that Your Excellency forward to the Executive Power the attached Indication, suggesting the creation of the Federal University of the City of Goiás-GO, through the dismemberment of the Federal University of Goiás.

Session Room, October 28, 2009. - Deputy Pedro Wilson, Rapporteur.

INDICATION No. , 2009
(From the Committee on Education and Culture)
Suggests the creation of the Federal University of the City of Goiás-GO, through the dismemberment of the Federal University of Goiás.

Excelentissimo Mr. Minister of State for Education:

The Committee on Education and Culture of the Chamber of Deputies examined, at its meeting on October 28, 2009, the Project of Law No. 2,723, of 2007, originating from the Federal Senate, of Senator Marconi Perillo (PSDB-GO), which authorizes the Executive Power to create the Federal University of the City of Goiás-GO, through the dismemberment of the Federal University of Goiás.

Due to its Resolution No. 1, of 2001, of Recommendation to Rapporteurs, the Committee decided to reject the project, not for lack of merit of content, but in accordance with the aforementioned Resolution.
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES

due to the formal inadequacy of its presentation as a bill.

The consistent justification of the aforementioned bill led this Commission to decide on forwarding this Indication to Your Excellency, in order to suggest its inclusion in the plans for the expansion of the federal network of higher education, currently being implemented by this Ministry.

In his justification, the author of the proposal, Senator Marconi Perillo, justifies the creation of a new university in the northwest of the state of Goiás, highlighting that the necessary infrastructure conditions for the installation of this educational unit already exist, as the Federal University of Goiás already maintains an extension in the city of Goiás, where the Law Bachelor's course operates.

It is also worth noting that this proposal aligns with the education policy of the Ministry of Education (MEC) of decentralization of higher education, through the installation of new universities or campuses of existing universities, as a way to ensure access to knowledge for a larger portion of the population living away from the major urban centers, where the largest offer of higher education vacancies in our country is concentrated.

Therefore, when forwarding this Indication, the Education and Culture Commission (CEC) is fully convinced that Your Excellency will make all the necessary efforts to attend to this important request from the Goianese population, thus contributing to the socio-economic growth of this city, which, due to its historical importance and notable colonial heritage, is considered by UNESCO a Cultural Heritage of Humanity since 2001.

Chamber of Sessions, October 28, 2009. - Deputy Pedro Wilson, Rapporteur.

I – Report
Bill No. 2,723, 2007, aims to authorize the Executive Branch to establish the Federal University of the City of Goiás, with its seat and forum in the Municipality of Goiás, through the dismemberment of the Federal University of Goiás, to provide higher education, conduct research in various fields of knowledge, and promote university extension. This proposal has been processed by the Committee on Labor, Administration and Public Service – CTASP and by the Committee on Education and Culture – CEC, having been unanimously approved by the latter and rejected by the latter, in accordance with the Summary of Recommendations to Rapporteurs No. 01/2001 – CEC/Chamber of Deputies, which deals with the evaluation of projects of a purely authorizing nature for the creation of educational institutions. Such a position
has been adopted by this collegiate body, as proposals
of this nature, of parliamentary initiative, invade the
exclusive competence of the President of the Republic,
in accordance with Article 61, §1, item II of the Federal
Constitution. This is the report.

It is the responsibility of the Commission on Finance and Taxation
to examine the proposal, in accordance with Article 32, item X,
subitem “h” of the Internal Regulation of this House and the
Internal Norms of the Commission on Finance and Taxation,
of May 29, 1996, regarding the compatibility or adequacy
of its provisions with the Multi-annual Plan (MPP),
the Law of Budgetary Guidelines (LBO), the Annual Budget
(LOA), and other legal provisions in force.

Preliminarily, it is worth noting that the bill under review
violates Article 61, §1, item II, subitem “e” of the Federal
Constitution. This provision stipulates that the initiative
for a law aimed at creating public administration bodies
is an exclusive attribute of the President of the Republic. At this step, Article 8 of the Internal Norms of the Finance and Taxation Commission, which establishes procedures for examining budget and financial compatibility or appropriateness, states that "a proposal that increases [...] will be considered incompatible."

"expenses related to exclusive initiatives of the President of the Republic" (I have emphasized this).

It is also verified that the proposal under analysis, in the light of Article 17 of the Fiscal Responsibility Law - LRF (Complementary Law No. 101/2000), establishes for the entity a legal obligation for a period exceeding two exercises, constituting a continuous mandatory expense. Thus, according to § 1 of the aforementioned provision, "acts that create or increase the expense referred to in the caput shall be accompanied by the estimate provided for in Article 16, Item I, and demonstrate the source of resources for its financing." Article 16, Item I, stipulates:

Art. 16. The creation, expansion or improvement of a governmental action that entails an increase in expenses shall be accompanied by:

The Author justifies his proposal by arguing that it is important to seek a sustainable mining policy, focusing on business, economic, social, and environmental issues, in order to make economic development harmonious.

II – Relator's Vote
Despite the noble Author's concerns for harmonious and sustainable economic development and the significant interests for national security, we cannot agree with the proposals presented here.

First, because although mineral reserves are finite, their exploitation triggers a series of other economic activities that allow mining states and municipalities, as well as their inhabitants, to earn revenues from diverse sources, making them more independent from mining activities and, when the mineral deposits are exhausted, they will already have their economic development secured through the continuity and diversification of economic activities on their respective territories.

Second, because it is necessary to avoid dispersing resources from a particular economic activity to other unrelated areas; for this, there are other sources of resources, in addition to governmental planning and budget allocations that should, by right, be allocated to them.

Therefore, this Relator does not see a compelling reason to approve the proposals under examination; thus, he has no other choice but to vote against Bill No. 3,854, of 2008, as well as against its attached proposal, Bill No. 3,878, of 2008, and to request his esteemed colleagues on this Committee to follow his vote.

Mr. Minister: We have no doubt that education and the expansion of the offer of educational and professional formation of excellent level constitute the privileged strategy to dynamize a country, contributing greatly to regional and local socio-economic development.
With this in mind, we have been closely monitoring, since December 2005, the progress of the Plan for the Expansion of the Federal Network of Professional and Technological Education, which has been implemented by the Ministry of Education (MEC).
In its first stage, to be completed in 2006, the Plan allocated to the state of Amazonas only one new technical education unit - a UNED to be installed in Coari, derived from the pre-existing CEFET in the state. The work suffered significant delays and its construction schedule had to be postponed to 2007.
When the PDE - Program for the Development of Education - was launched in April 2007, which, among other things, provided for the installation, within four years, of 150 (one hundred and fifty) technical schools in pole cities chosen by the government, the MEC announced that phase 2 of the Expansion Plan had begun. In this second stage, Amazonas was to be provided with five technical/technological education units to be installed in LÁBREA, MAUÉS, PARINTINS, PRESIDENTE FIGUEIREDO and TABATINGA, according to a schedule that would unfold during 2008/2010.
However, in August 2008, the government decided to send to Congress a bill creating 38 (thirty-eight) IFETs - Federal Institutes of Education, Science and Technology in the country, based on the federal network of professional education, a bill that, after becoming Federal Law No. 11892 in December 2008, absorbed and reordered, in a new agenda, all the former technical and technological education units (such as CEFETs and Technical Schools) and also the new ones, the subject of the aforementioned Expansion Plan. Present in all states, the IFETs are already or will be responsible for offering integrated secondary education with professional training, technology higher education courses, engineering bachelor's degrees and teaching licenses.
In this new scenario created with the sanction of the new Law, the situation in Amazonas was as follows: the state was provided with one IFET - the Federal Institute of Amazonas, integrated by the campuses of Manaus - Centro, Manaus - Zona Leste, Manaus - Distrito Industrial, São Gabriel da Cachoeira (Federal Agrotécnic School), and the units that previously integrated the Expansion Plan 2007/2010 - Coari

Based on a proper plan and an implementation schedule to be followed in coordination with the other technical units planned for installation in the Amazon region, this proposal, eagerly awaited especially by young people and productive sectors of the state and region, could become a reality.

We therefore wish to join the noble Senators of the Republic who today support this good proposal to expand the Brazilian university network, and knowing the public spirit that guides their decisions and actions at the helm of the MEC, we believe we can also count on the support of Your Excellency in advancing this cause.

Thus, on this occasion, we respectfully request that Your Excellency take the necessary steps, in collaboration with the competent technical sectors of the Ministry of Education and other government agencies, to inaugurate as soon as possible a new Technological Education Center in Manacapuru, in the state of Amazonas. This new institution will undoubtedly bring the dynamism so necessary to the Amazon interior and also, let us not forget, to Northern Brazil.

We express our certainty that we can count on Your Excellency's collaboration in embracing and implementing this proposal, which reflects the aspirations of the population of the state of Amazonas. Believe Your Excellency that the creation of another federal technological education unit in the Northern region of the country will open the way to a more dignified life for thousands and thousands of young Brazilians.
