COMMITTEE ON FINANCE AND TAXATION

I – Report

Bill No. 4,105, of 2008, aims to authorize the Executive Branch to establish the Federal Center for Technological Education of Manacapuru, linked to the Ministry of Education, with headquarters in the municipality of Manacapuru, in the state of Amazonas, with the objective of training and qualifying higher-level professionals to meet the socio-economic needs of the state of Amazonas and neighboring states, as well as to contribute to the country's technological development.

The proposal was processed by the Committee on Labor, Administration, and Public Service – CTASP and by the Committee on Education and Culture – CEC, having been unanimously approved by that body and rejected by the latter, in accordance with the Summary of Recommendations to Relators No. 01/2001 – CEC/Chamber of Deputies, which deals with the evaluation of projects of a purely authorizing nature for the creation of educational institutions. This position has been adopted by this collegiate body as proposals of this nature, of parliamentary initiative, invade the exclusive competence of the President of the Republic, in accordance with Article 61, § 1, Item II of the Federal Constitution.

This is the report.

II – Vote

It is the responsibility of the Committee on Finance and Taxation to evaluate the proposal, in accordance with Article 54, Item II, of the Internal Regulation of this House and the Internal Norm of the Committee on Finance and Taxation, of May 29, 1996, regarding the compatibility or adequacy of its provisions with the Multi-Annual Plan (PPA).
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES

The Budget Guidelines Law (LDO), with the annual budget (LOA) and other legal provisions in force.

Preliminarily, it is noted that the bill under examination violates Article 61, § 1, item II, subitem “e” of the Federal Constitution. This provision stipulates that the initiative for a law establishing public administration bodies is a exclusive attribute of the President of the Republic.

At this point, Article 8 of the Internal Rules of the Commission on Finance and Taxation, which establishes procedures for examining budget and financial compatibility or adequacy, states that “a proposal that increases expenditure in matters of exclusive initiative of the President of the Republic will be considered incompatible” (emphasis added).

It is also verified that the proposal under review, in the light of Article 17 of the Fiscal Responsibility Law (LRF - Complementary Law No. 101/2000), imposes a legal obligation on the entity for a period exceeding two fiscal years, constituting a continuous mandatory expenditure. Thus, according to § 1 of the aforementioned provision, “acts that create or increase expenditure referred to in the caput shall be accompanied by the estimate provided for in Article 16, item I, and demonstrate the source of resources for its financing.” Article 16, item I, stipulates:

Article 16. The creation, expansion, or improvement of government action that entails an increase in expenditure shall be accompanied by:

I – an estimate of the budgetary and financial impact in the exercise in which it is to enter into force and in the two subsequent ones.

In the same sense, Law No. 12,309 of August 9, 2010 (LDO 2011) provides:

Article 91. Legislative proposals, in the form of bills, legislative decrees, or provisional measures, that involve or authorize a decrease in Union revenue or an increase in expenditure for the 2011 exercise, shall be accompanied by estimates of these effects for each of the exercises included in the period from 2011 to 2013, detailing the respective calculation memorandum and corresponding compensation, in accordance with the constitutional and legal provisions that govern the matter.

In support of the understanding of the aforementioned provisions, the Commission on Finance and Taxation issued Summary No. 1 of 2008, which considers incompatible and inadequate a proposal, even if of an authorizing nature, that fails to estimate the budgetary and financial impact and demonstrate the source of resources for its financing, as follows:

SUMMARY No. 1/08-CFT – It is incompatible and inadequate to propose, even in an authorizing character, that, conflicting with the norms of Law Complementary No. 101, of May 4, 2000 – Fiscal Responsibility Law – fails to present the estimate of its budgetary and financial impact as well as the respective compensation.

As for the examination of the proposal's adequacy with the Multi-annual Plan – PPA 2008-2011, it is found that there is no specific action for the creation of a Federal Center of Technological Education in the city of Manacapuru, State of Amazonas, in Program 1062 – Development of Professional and Technological Education. In turn, the Annual Budget Law – LOA 2011 does not provide resources for this initiative.

In view of the above, I submit to this collegial body my vote for the incompatibility with budgetary and financial norms and for the budgetary and financial inadequacy of Law Project No. 4.105, of 2008.

I – Report
Bill No. 4,705, of 2009, authorizes the Executive

the municipality of Tabatinga, in the state of Amazonas,
in accordance with Law No. 11,508, of July 20, 2007.
Export Processing Zones have encouraged the

This Commission, in addition to examining the

its compatibility or adequacy with the multi-annual
plan,

The Budget Guidelines Law and the Annual Budget, in accordance with the Internal Rules of the Chamber of Deputies (RI, arts. 32, IX, “h” and 53, II) and the Internal Norms of the Commission on Finance and Taxation, which "establishes procedures for the examination of budget or financial suitability," approved by CFT on May 29, 1996.

The Budget Guidelines Law of 2011 (Law No. 12.309, of August 9, 2010), in its Article 91, conditions the approval of legislative proposals, in the form of bills, legislative decrees, or provisional measures, that involve or authorize a decrease in revenue or an increase in expenditure for the Union, on the presentation of estimates of these effects, prepared or approved by a Union agency, for each of the exercises included in the period from 2011 to 2013, detailing the respective calculation memory and corresponding compensation, in accordance with the constitutional and legal provisions that govern the matter. Legislative proposals that grant or expand financial, credit, or patrimonial incentives or benefits must contain a clause of validity of no more than 5 years, and their compensation may be made by canceling expenses equivalent in value.

Still in its Article 91, the 2011 BGL highlights that the reference to future legislation, the installment or postponement to future exercises of the budgetary-financial impact does not eliminate the necessary estimate and corresponding compensation.

Article 14 of the Fiscal Responsibility Law - LRF requires that the proposal be accompanied by an estimate of the budgetary-financial impact for the exercise in which it is intended to come into effect and for the following two exercises, as well as its compatibility with the fulfillment of the fiscal goals established in the Budget Guidelines Law and the achievement of at least one of two alternative conditions.

One condition is that the proposer demonstrates that the waiver was considered in the revenue estimate of the budgetary law and will not affect the fiscal results goals provided in the specific annex of the Budget Guidelines Law. Another alternative condition is that the proposal be accompanied by compensation measures, during the mentioned period, through the increase in revenue from the increase in rates, the expansion of the calculation base, or the increase or creation of a tax or contribution, and the benefit may only come into effect when such measures are implemented.

Bill No. 4.705, of 2009, authorizes the Executive Branch to create a Special Export Processing Zone in the Municipality of Tabatinga, in the state of Amazonas. The creation of a ZPE generates fiscal waiver, as established in Article 14, Item III, of the Fiscal Responsibility Law.

COMMISSION ON EDUCATION AND CULTURE

I – Report

The Senate Bill under consideration was presented in that House of Congress by the noble Senator Jayme Campos in October 2007 and approved, with final decision, by the Senate's Commission on Education, Culture, and Sports in March 2009.

The proposal in question authorizes the Executive Branch to establish the Federal University of Northern Mato Grosso (UFENORTE), with its seat in the municipality of Sinop, in the state of Mato Grosso, as well as the positions, jobs, and functions necessary for its operation.

It stipulates that UFENORTE's objectives will be to provide higher education, conduct research in various fields of knowledge, and promote university extension, and that its organizational structure and mode of operation will be defined in its statute, observing the principle of the indissociability between teaching, research, and extension.

Finally, it establishes that the installation of this new higher education institution will be contingent upon the prior allocation, in the Union Budget, of the necessary budgetary provisions for its operation.

Distributed to the Commissions on Labor, Administration, and Public Service; Education and Culture; Finance and Taxation; and Constitution and Justice and Citizenship of this House of Congress, the present proposal is subject to the conclusive consideration of the commissions.

In the Commission on Labor, Administration, and Public Service, the present Senate Bill received a favorable report from the noble Deputada Thelma de Oliveira, approved unanimously at a regular meeting of that Commission on December 16, 2009.
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES

In the Education and Culture Commission, with the regulatory deadline open, no amendments were presented to the bill under consideration.

II – Relator's Vote
In justifying his bill, the distinguished Senator Jayme Campos argues that policies aimed at valuing the Amazon region have been promoting significant development in the North region of the State of Mato Grosso.

As a result of this development process, the Federal University of Mato Grosso (UFMT) established a campus in that region with nine undergraduate courses, six regular courses (Agriculture, Nursing, Forest Engineering, Veterinary Medicine, Zoology, and Full Degree in Natural Sciences and Mathematics) and three special courses (Biological Sciences, Accounting Sciences, and Physical Education).

However, there is currently a latent demand for higher education vacancies in the region, as there are approximately 34,000 enrollments in secondary education, while only slightly over a thousand vacancies are available in undergraduate courses.

The proposal to create a new federal university in the North region of Mato Grosso, based on the installations of the UFMT campus in Sinop, aims to respond to this demand by expanding access to higher education in a region of the state composed of 43 Mato Grosso municipalities.

It thus meets the imperative of regional economic and social development, generating employment, income, and training professionals at the higher education level, particularly in the health and education sectors.

Despite the undeniable merit of the proposal, it is necessary to consider the observations contained in the Summary of Recommendations to the Relators of the Education and Culture Commission No. 1/2001 - CEC, reaffirmed on April 25, 2007, which establishes criteria for the analysis of certain types of initiatives.

The Summary stipulates that, regarding proposals related to the creation or transformation of a federal school at any level or mode of instruction, the recommendation to the Relators is that the opinion conclude by rejecting the proposal. Since the creation of federal schools implies the creation of public bodies and, consequently, of corresponding positions, functions, and jobs, such legislative initiative, according to Article 61, § 1, II, of the Federal Constitution, is exclusive to the Executive branch. The creation or transformation of an educational institution should be suggested in

**INDICATION TO THE EXECUTIVE BRANCH, IN ACCORDANCE WITH ARTICLE 113 OF THE RULES OF THIS HOUSE.** For this reason, we advocate the rejection of House Bill No. 5,157, of 2009. However, recognizing the merit of the proposal under consideration, and in order to ensure that its objective is not lost, we suggest its submission in the form of an Indication from this Education and Culture Committee to the Executive Branch. I – Report

and other legal provisions in force.
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES

Preliminarily, it is relevant to note that the bill under examination violates Article 61, § 1, item II, subitem "e" of the Federal Constitution. This provision stipulates that the initiative for legislation aimed at creating public administration bodies is a sole prerogative of the President of the Republic.

At this point, Article 8 of the Internal Norms of the Finance and Taxation Committee, which establishes procedures for examining budget and financial compatibility or adequacy, states that "a proposal that increases expenditure in matters of exclusive initiative of the President of the Republic will be considered incompatible" (emphasis added).

Furthermore, the analysis of the proposal, in light of Article 17 of the Fiscal Responsibility Law - LRF (Complementary Law No. 101/2000), establishes a legal obligation for the entity for a period exceeding two fiscal years, constituting a continuous mandatory expenditure. Thus, as per § 1 of the aforementioned article, "acts that create or increase expenditure referred to in the caput shall be accompanied by the estimate provided for in Article 16, item I, and demonstrate the source of resources for its financing." Article 16, item I, stipulates:

Art. 16. The creation, expansion, or improvement of government action that entails an increase in expenditure shall be accompanied by:
I - an estimate of the budgetary and financial impact in the exercise in which it is to enter into force and in the two subsequent ones.

In the same vein, Law No. 12,309 of August 9, 2010 (LDO 2011) provides:

Art. 91. Legislative proposals, in the form of bills, legislative decrees, or provisional measures, that involve or authorize a decrease in Union revenue or an increase in expenditure for the 2011 fiscal year shall be accompanied by estimates of these effects for each of the exercises included in the period from 2011 to 2013, detailing the respective calculation memorandum and corresponding compensation, in accordance with the constitutional and legal provisions that govern the matter.

In corroboration with the understanding of the aforementioned provisions, the Finance and Taxation Committee issued Summary No. 1 of 2008, which considers incompatible and inadequate a proposal, even in an authorizing character, that conflicts with the LRF by failing to estimate the budgetary and financial impact and demonstrate the source of resources for its financing, as stated as follows:

SUMMARY NO. 1/08-CFT - A proposal, even in an authorizing character, is considered incompatible and inadequate if it fails to estimate the budgetary and financial impact and demonstrate the source of resources for its financing.

Similarly, the Annual Budget Law - LOA 2011 does not provide resources for this initiative.

However, both documents have the allocation "12.364.1073.1H69.0101 - Expansion of Higher Education - Campus of Sinop", indicating the intention of the Federal Government to establish a new campus in the aforementioned Mato Grosso municipality, instead of creating a new Federal University.

In light of the above, I submit to this body my vote against the compatibility with budgetary and financial norms and against the budgetary and financial inadequacy of Project of Law No. 5,157, of 2009.

BILL NO. 7.052-A, 2010
(From Mr. Cleber Verde)
Adds articles 37-A and 37 B to Law
No. 8.078, of September 11, 1990, to
provide for misleading advertising via
the Internet, deceptive telemarketing,
spams (unsolicited messages), in the
publicity of consumer credit offers
in interest-free installments; with a
Defense of the Consumer Commission
report recommending rejection (report
author: DEP. CÉSAR HALUM).
Ruling: To the Defense of the Consumer
and Constitution and Citizenship Commissions
(Art. 54 RICD)
Consideration: Proposal Subject to
Conclusive Consideration by the Commissions – Art. 24 II
Publication of the Defense of the Consumer
Commission report
I – Report
Bill No. 7.052, 2010, proposes adding two new
provisions to the Consumer Defense Code – CDC
to address issues related to the advertising of
consumer credit offers through the global computer
network – the Internet.
The first new proposed provision, article 37-A,
aims to prohibit all misleading advertising via the
Internet, deceptive marketing, and spams.
The second proposed provision, article 37-B,
seeks to penalize the credit provider when they
offer their product as being interest-free and
without other fees.
II – Report of the Relator
The bill under consideration has the undeniable
merit of seeking to defend and protect the Brazilian
consumer who uses the global computer network –
the Internet, as well as the consumer of financing
and loans in general.
However, we cannot fail to recognize that the
problem that the proposed legislation seeks to address
is already regulated in the CDC itself.
Regarding misleading advertising, let us look at
what article 37 of Law No. 8.078, 1990, states:

“Article 37. Misleading or abusive advertising
is prohibited.
§ 1. Misleading advertising includes any form
of information or promotional communication,
completely or partially false, or, in any other
way, even by omission, misleading...

Peace of deceiving the consumer regarding
the nature, characteristics, quality, quantity,
properties, origin, price, and any other data
about products and services.
§ 2. Unfair practices include, among others,
discriminatory advertising of any nature,
inciting violence, exploiting fear or superstition,
taking advantage of a child's lack of judgment
and experience, disregarding environmental
values, or inducing the consumer to behave in
a way that is harmful or dangerous to their health
or safety.
§ 3. For the purposes of this code, advertising
is misleading by omission when it fails to inform
about an essential aspect of the product or service.

As for the information disclosed in the offer of
products or services, including financial services,
let's look at what articles 30 and 31 of the Consumer
Protection Code state:

"Article 30. Any information or advertising,
sufficiently accurate, disseminated through any
form or means of communication regarding
products and services offered or presented,
obliges the supplier who disseminates or uses it,
and forms part of the contract that may be concluded.

Article 31. The offer and presentation of
products or services must provide correct, clear,
accurate, conspicuous, and in Portuguese language
information about their characteristics, qualities,
quantity, composition, price, warranty, shelf life,
and origin, among other data, as well as about the
risks they pose to consumers' health and safety." (our emphasis)

As we can see, the Consumer Protection Code
already has sufficient regulation to establish as a
consumer violation the situations that the proposed
bill aims to address.

The problem is not the lack of law or regulatory
norms, the problem is the lack of enforcement and
application of the law. More importantly, it is
something that unfortunately has not been happening
in our country: the judiciary allowing the payment
of fair and high enough compensation to deter
violators from continuing to ignore consumer protection
legislation.

In light of the above, considering the existing
general regulation on the proposed matter, we
recommend rejecting Project of Law No. 7,052,
of 2010.

Chamber of the Commission, June 1, 2011. - Deputy
César Halum, Rapporteur.

National identity is constructed from the various identities forged in every corner of Brazil. As noted by the noble author of the proposal, Stei-
nhaeger, a distilled beverage produced in Porto União,
has received certification from the Beverage Tasting Institute in Chicago, USA, achieving 89 points on a 100-point scale. Produced craftily, this alcoholic beverage from Porto União retains the originality and purity of the German formula, with precise measurements of cereal spirits, juniper berries, roots, seeds, and rinds.

On the other hand, Xixo—another name for the well-known carne assada on a skewer—has different ethnic references. Skewers are made in various ways and compositions: in China, for example, pork skewers have been prepared for approximately 800 years. In Japan, the most common is the bird's meat skewer marinated in soy sauce; in the Syrian-Lebanese culture, they make a lamb michuê; the Arabs make shish, which means skewer; in Russia and countries with Turkish influence, there is chechelick, which was likely one of the first skewers commercially introduced in Brazil. In Porto União, making a xixada means preparing a "churrasquinho" (small barbecue) of beef on a wire skewer with a loop at one end, roasting it on a grill.

In Porto União, you can find the delicious Xixo, which is the main attraction at parties, gatherings, and get-togethers among friends. Xixo is considered an intangible cultural heritage of Porto União.

Consuming Stei-nhaeger and Xixo and taking pride in the quality of these products in the city has become a habit that is part of the cultural identity of a native of Porto União, in Santa Catarina. In light of this, I vote in favor of the approval of Law Project No. 7.075, 2010.

In his justification, the distinguished author of the proposal in question emphasizes that the figure of the Individual Entrepreneur, created by Law Complementary No. 128 of 2008, is fundamental for job creation and income generation, and consequently, for the country's economic growth, bringing thousands of informal workers who are marginalized from labor rights and benefits into the light.

The proposed commemorative date to honor the Individual Entrepreneur is July 1st, the day on which the legal changes that established this category came into effect.

Law Complementary No. 128 of 2008 created special conditions for workers known as informal to become legally recognized Individual Entrepreneurs. Thus, people who work for themselves as artisans, merchants, hairdressers, truck drivers, small manufacturers, masons, painters, service providers, etc., can establish themselves as small entrepreneurs, enrolled in the Simplified National System (Simples Nacional), and start contributing to Social Security and ICMS or ISS.

With this initiative, thousands of workers can gain access to social security coverage, banking services, and special credit lines, including technical support from the Brazilian Service of Support for Micro and Small Businesses (Sebrae) to organize their businesses. The main benefit of this measure is, essentially, to strengthen the sense of citizenship among these workers by restoring their dignity and personal, professional, and social fulfillment.

Since the end of 2010, Law No. 12.345 has been in force, establishing criteria for the establishment of commemorative dates. It also defines that proposals with this objective should be accompanied by evidence of consultations and/or public hearings with broad sectors of the population, in order to meet the criterion of great significance for different segments of society. The approval of the proposal under review represents an exception to that rule.

**Publication of the Opinion of the Education and Culture Commission**

**I – Report**

The examined bill, of noble Deputy Luiz Carlos Pitiman, deals with the care of children up to three years old in home-based day cares.

The proposal consists of eight articles, organized as follows:

Article 1 defines a home-based day care as one that operates in a residence, primarily catering to working mothers.

Article 2 provides that home-based day cares will be gradually replaced by permanent spaces created by municipalities.

Article 3 requires a complete elementary education and training with a minimum of twenty hours of instruction, to be provided by the education system, for individuals interested in working as "nursery mothers."

Article 4 stipulates that the number of children to be cared for in home-based day cares will depend on the conditions of the residence, to be regulated by the managing body.

Article 5 states that municipalities will pay a "financial aid" to nursery mothers, with the possibility of assistants to help them (Article 6).

Finally, Article 7 establishes that the municipality's technical bodies should provide assistance for socio-educational work, and Article 8 that the operating norms for home-based day cares will be defined by municipalities, in line with the goals of the National Education Plan.

In justifying his proposal, the author refers to the National Education Plan, currently under review in the Chamber of Deputies, which sets a goal of providing care to fifty percent of the population aged zero to three years old.

The proposal, which is being processed in accordance with Article 24, II, of the Internal Regulation, subject to the final opinion of the committees, has been submitted to the Education and Culture Commission for merit review, having received no amendments within the regulatory timeframe.

This is the report.

**II – Relator's Vote**

The purpose of the bill under review is to expand care for children from zero to three years old through home-based day cares, characterized as those operating in residences and under the responsibility of the so-called "nursery mother." This form of care would, according to Article 2, be supplemented by permanent spaces created by municipalities.

It is commendable and absolutely timely the concern demonstrated by the distinguished Deputy Luiz Pitiman. After all, it is about facing the problem of expanding opportunities for care to approximately three million children aged zero to three years in the next ten years, as determined by Goal No. 1 of the National Education Plan proposal sent by the Executive Power to the National Congress.

From the perspective of this Education Commission, it is necessary to analyze the proposal from the perspective of the right to education and the demands and characteristics of the Brazilian educational system. So let's see:

Early childhood education is a right, to take place in creche and preschool for children up to five years of age, as determined by Article 208, Item IV of the Federal Constitution. In accordance with Article 29 of the Law of Guidelines and Bases of National Education, early childhood education is considered the first stage of basic education, with the purpose of promoting the integral development of the child, "in its physical, psychological, intellectual and social aspects, complementing the action of the family and the community."

On the other hand, the Brazilian educational system is institutional, school-based, meaning that the formal education to be offered by the state must take place in specific institutions characterized as educational establishments. These institutions must adhere to a set of norms and procedures specific to them, established in a concurrent manner by the Union, States, and Municipalities.

I would like to highlight, by way of example, the need for educational action to be preceded by a collective and systematized political-pedagogical project, which should involve teachers and families. Another example is the requirement established in Article 62 of the LDB that professionals dedicated to performing pedagogical work must be trained at the higher education level, in a bachelor's degree course, with the possibility of training at the medium-level normal school to work in early childhood education and the initial years of fundamental education.

"Home creche" breaks with the concept that care for children up to five years old should take place in educational institutions. It represents, in this sense, a step backward in the historical struggle that this Congress has been the stage for - and whose victory was celebrated with the entry into force of the current LDB - to insert the educational right of early childhood as part of the basic education process, freeing it from the precarious social welfare actions that characterized it for decades.

There is also a need to record the possibility of financial aid to "creche mothers" and their assistants, as provided for in the bill. There are implications that must be considered in this proposal, such as the precariousness of labor rights and the assumption of potential legal liabilities. There is case law in Brazilian courts regarding the employment relationship between "creche mothers" and local governments. In one argument, the Regional Labor Tribunal (TRT/9th Region) states: "These (local governments) cannot want to remove from their shoulders the duty they have towards their citizens, transferring it to physical persons in exchange for some benefits, which are nothing more than 'in-kind' salaries."

It is imperative to find ways to democratize access to creches. Therefore, it is important to highlight the existence of the National Program for Restructuring and Acquisition of Equipment for the Public School Network of Early Childhood Education (Pró-Infância), funded by the Ministry of Education, which provides for the construction of six thousand creches and preschools by 2014. Numerous city halls are also trying to find ways to expand services for early childhood education.

As we explore these paths, it will be essential to keep in mind that the right to education is fulfilled not only through quantitative expansion of services, but through a quality offer that effectively addresses the needs of a decisive phase in the development of future generations of Brazil.

Given this, the vote is to reject PL No. 75, 2011.

Due to this constitutional provision, Law No. 7,990 of December 28, 1989 established financial compensation for the results of oil or natural gas exploration, water resources for electricity generation, and mineral resources in their respective territories, continental shelf, territorial sea or exclusive economic zone.
Governmental participations in the oil sector, including financial compensations, were detailed by Law No. 9,478 of August 6, 1997, in its Article 45. This article is transcribed below:
“Article 45. The concession contract shall provide for the following governmental participations, as specified in the bidding document:
I – signature bonus;
II – royalties;
III – special participation;
IV – payment for occupation or retention of area.”
Royalties and special participation, which are financial compensations, are the most significant governmental participations in monetary terms. Article 47 of Law No. 9.478/1997 and its paragraph 1, which establish the value of royalties, are described below:
“Article 47. Royalties shall be paid monthly, in national currency, from the date of commencement of commercial production of each field, in an amount corresponding to ten percent of the production of oil or natural gas.
§ 1. Taking into account geological risks, production expectations and other relevant factors, the ANP may, in the corresponding bidding document, provide for a reduction in the value of royalties established in the main part of this article to an amount corresponding to at least five percent of production.”
It thus follows that royalties can vary from 5% to 10% of the value of oil or natural gas production.
The conditions for the collection of the special participation related to oil and natural gas production are established in Article 50 of Law No. 9.478/1997, as transcribed below:
